qualifiers.shift: Brief gelling of minutes suits osteoarthritis; prolonged morning stiffness beyond an hour suits inflammatory disease.

qualifiers.name: DIP-sparing
qualifiers.established: Examine the distal interphalangeal joints specifically
qualifiers.example: DIP-sparing polyarthritis → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: A clean discriminator. RA spares the DIPs; osteoarthritis and psoriatic arthritis characteristically involve them.

qualifiers.name: Sicca
qualifiers.established: Ask about dry eyes and mouth; Schirmer test if needed
qualifiers.example: sicca symptoms → Sjögren syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Prompts anti-Ro and anti-La testing and raises the associated risks of renal tubular acidosis and lymphoma.

qualifiers.name: Large-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.established: Four-limb blood pressures, bruits, and vascular imaging
qualifiers.example: limb claudication with blood pressure discrepancy → Takayasu arteritis
qualifiers.shift: Predicts limb claudication, bruits, blood pressure discrepancies, and aortic complications, and points to imaging of the aorta rather than tissue biopsy of small vessels.

qualifiers.name: Medium-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.definition: Main visceral arteries and their branches
qualifiers.established: Angiography or biopsy of an affected organ
qualifiers.example: renal microaneurysms with mononeuritis → polyarteritis nodosa
qualifiers.shift: Predicts aneurysms, infarcts, and mononeuritis multiplex. Notably spares glomeruli, so glomerulonephritis argues against classic polyarteritis nodosa.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed when glomerulonephritis is present, which argues against it

qualifiers.name: Small-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.established: Skin or renal biopsy plus ANCA serology
qualifiers.example: palpable purpura with hematuria → ANCA-associated vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: Predicts palpable purpura, glomerulonephritis, and alveolar hemorrhage. The pulmonary-renal syndrome lives here.

qualifiers.name: Pauci-immune
qualifiers.definition: Little or no immune complex deposition on immunofluorescence
qualifiers.established: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence
qualifiers.example: pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis → ANCA vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: Separates ANCA vasculitis from immune complex disease and from anti-GBM disease on the same biopsy, which drives entirely different treatment.

qualifiers.name: Low complement
qualifiers.definition: Reduced C3 and C4 from consumption
qualifiers.established: Serum C3 and C4
qualifiers.associated: Lupus nephritis, post-infectious GN, cryoglobulinemia, endocarditis
qualifiers.example: low C3 and C4 with nephritis → lupus nephritis
qualifiers.shift: One of the most efficient discriminators in nephritis. Low complement narrows a long differential to a short one; normal complement points elsewhere, including ANCA vasculitis and IgA nephropathy.

qualifiers.name: Negatively birefringent
qualifiers.definition: Yellow when parallel to the compensator axis
qualifiers.established: Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid
qualifiers.example: negatively birefringent needles → gout
qualifiers.shift: Definitive for gout on synovial fluid. Note that crystals and infection can coexist, so their presence does not exclude septic arthritis.
qualifiers.misuse: Crystals do not exclude coexisting infection; always send fluid for culture too

qualifiers.name: Positively birefringent
qualifiers.definition: Blue when parallel to the compensator axis
qualifiers.established: Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid
qualifiers.example: positively birefringent rhomboids → calcium pyrophosphate deposition
qualifiers.shift: Identifies calcium pyrophosphate deposition, which should prompt evaluation for hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, and hypomagnesemia in younger patients.
qualifiers.misuse: Accepted as the final answer in a young patient without screening for hemochromatosis or hyperparathyroidism

qualifiers.name: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.definition: Skin thickening distal to elbows and knees, plus face
qualifiers.established: Map the proximal extent of skin thickening
qualifiers.example: limited cutaneous sclerosis → pulmonary arterial hypertension risk
qualifiers.shift: Predicts pulmonary arterial hypertension as the dominant late risk and a lower risk of scleroderma renal crisis.

qualifiers.name: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.definition: Skin thickening proximal to elbows and knees, including trunk
qualifiers.established: Map skin involvement proximal to elbows and knees or on the trunk
qualifiers.example: diffuse cutaneous sclerosis → scleroderma renal crisis risk
qualifiers.shift: Predicts interstitial lung disease and scleroderma renal crisis, and warrants blood pressure surveillance and early lung screening.
qualifiers.misuse: Blood pressure not monitored, which is how renal crisis is missed

qualifiers.name: Nailfold capillary abnormality
qualifiers.definition: Dilated loops and dropout on capillaroscopy
qualifiers.established: Dermatoscope or ophthalmoscope at the cuticle
qualifiers.example: abnormal nailfold capillaries → secondary Raynaud from systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Separates secondary from primary Raynaud phenomenon at the bedside with a simple magnifier, and predicts progression to a connective tissue disease.

qualifiers.name: Tophaceous
qualifiers.definition: Palpable deposits of urate in soft tissue
qualifiers.established: Inspection and palpation of ears, elbows, and digits
qualifiers.example: tophi over the helix and olecranon → chronic untreated gout
qualifiers.shift: Indicates a large total urate burden, mandates urate-lowering therapy, and requires a lower serum urate target than non-tophaceous disease.

qualifiers.name: Degenerative
qualifiers.established: Radiographs showing joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis
qualifiers.example: degenerative changes on radiograph → osteoarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Points away from inflammatory arthropathy. Note that degenerative change is near-universal with age, so its presence does not explain a patient's pain by itself
qualifiers.misuse: Radiographic degeneration reported as the cause of symptoms; prevalence in asymptomatic adults is very high

qualifiers.name: Blanching
qualifiers.established: Press with a glass slide or fingertip
qualifiers.example: blanching maculopapular rash → viral exanthem
qualifiers.shift: Vasodilation rather than extravasation. Generally reassuring and moves away from vasculitis and thrombocytopenia.

qualifiers.name: Nonblanching
qualifiers.established: Glass slide or diascopy over the lesion
qualifiers.example: nonblanching petechial rash with fever → meningococcemia
qualifiers.shift: The most urgent qualifier in dermatology. With fever it triggers immediate empiric therapy for meningococcemia; otherwise it directs toward thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.
qualifiers.misuse: Not tested at all; the single most important bedside maneuver in a febrile rash

qualifiers.name: Macular
qualifiers.established: Inspection and palpation for elevation
qualifiers.example: macular eruption → drug or viral exanthem
qualifiers.shift: Flat lesions imply a process in the epidermis or dermis without significant infiltrate or fluid.

qualifiers.name: Papular
qualifiers.established: Palpation confirming raised solid lesions
qualifiers.example: papular eruption → arthropod bites or drug eruption
qualifiers.shift: Implies a dermal cellular infiltrate.

qualifiers.name: Maculopapular
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus timing relative to drug exposure
qualifiers.example: maculopapular eruption after a new drug → drug exanthem
qualifiers.shift: The most common inpatient rash. The key branch point is timing relative to drug exposure and the presence of fever, eosinophilia, or mucosal involvement.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed benign without checking for eosinophilia, mucosal involvement, or organ dysfunction

qualifiers.name: Vesicular
qualifiers.established: Inspection; PCR of vesicle fluid if uncertain
qualifiers.example: grouped vesicles on an erythematous base → herpes simplex or zoster
qualifiers.shift: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base is herpetic. Distribution then separates zoster from disseminated infection.

qualifiers.name: Bullous
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus Nikolsky testing and mucosal examination
qualifiers.example: tense bullae in an elderly patient → bullous pemphigoid
qualifiers.shift: Raises the blistering emergencies. Mucosal involvement plus a positive Nikolsky sign is a dermatologic emergency.

qualifiers.name: Pustular
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus culture to establish sterility
qualifiers.example: sterile pustules → acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
qualifiers.shift: Neutrophilic. Sterile pustules suggest pustular psoriasis or AGEP rather than infection.

qualifiers.name: Petechial
qualifiers.established: Diascopy plus urgent platelet count
qualifiers.example: petechiae → thrombocytopenia
qualifiers.shift: Mandates an immediate platelet count and, with fever, empiric antibiotics before results.

qualifiers.name: Purpuric
qualifiers.established: Diascopy and palpation for elevation
qualifiers.example: purpuric lesions → vasculitis or coagulopathy
qualifiers.shift: Palpable purpura specifically indicates small-vessel vasculitis and warrants a search for renal and pulmonary involvement.

qualifiers.name: Palpable purpura
qualifiers.definition: Purpura raised above the skin surface
qualifiers.established: Close the eyes and palpate; the elevation is the finding
qualifiers.example: palpable purpura → small-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: The tactile quality is the diagnosis. Palpability implies inflammatory vessel wall infiltration rather than simple extravasation.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed by sight alone, which cannot detect palpability

qualifiers.name: Urticarial
qualifiers.established: Circle a lesion and reassess after 24 hours
qualifiers.example: wheals resolving within 24 hours → ordinary urticaria
qualifiers.shift: Individual lesions lasting under 24 hours is ordinary urticaria; lesions lasting longer, bruising, or burning rather than itching suggests urticarial vasculitis.
qualifiers.misuse: Persistent lesions called urticaria; longer than a day suggests urticarial vasculitis

qualifiers.name: Targetoid
qualifiers.established: Inspection for concentric zones
qualifiers.example: three-zone target lesions on the palms → erythema multiforme
qualifiers.shift: True three-zone targets on acral surfaces suggest erythema multiforme, most often HSV-driven.

qualifiers.name: Annular
qualifiers.established: Inspection of the border plus skin scraping for KOH
qualifiers.example: annular scaling plaque with central clearing → tinea corporis
qualifiers.shift: A scaling advancing border suggests dermatophyte; a non-scaling expanding ring after tick exposure suggests erythema migrans.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with topical steroid, which produces tinea incognito

qualifiers.name: Reticular
qualifiers.established: Inspection with attention to symmetry and completeness of the net
qualifiers.example: reticular mottling → livedo reticularis
qualifiers.shift: Implies impaired dermal microcirculation and prompts consideration of antiphospholipid syndrome, vasculitis, and emboli.

qualifiers.name: Confluent
qualifiers.established: Serial inspection documenting merging
qualifiers.example: confluent morbilliform eruption → measles or drug rash
qualifiers.shift: Progression from discrete to confluent generally indicates a worsening or evolving eruption.

qualifiers.name: Acral
qualifiers.established: Deliberately examine palms and soles
qualifiers.associated: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease, secondary syphilis, endocarditis lesions
qualifiers.example: palmar and plantar rash → secondary syphilis
qualifiers.shift: Palmar and plantar involvement narrows sharply: secondary syphilis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, and erythema multiforme.
qualifiers.misuse: Palms and soles not examined, which discards a very short differential

qualifiers.name: Flexural
qualifiers.established: Examine antecubital and popliteal fossae
qualifiers.example: flexural eczematous plaques → atopic dermatitis
qualifiers.shift: Flexural predominance in an atopic patient is eczema; extensor predominance is psoriasis. Distribution alone often resolves this pair.

qualifiers.name: Extensor
qualifiers.established: Examine elbows, knees, scalp, and nails
qualifiers.example: extensor plaques → psoriasis
qualifiers.shift: See above; the mirror image of flexural.

qualifiers.name: Photosensitive
qualifiers.established: Map the eruption against sun-exposed areas
qualifiers.example: malar rash sparing the nasolabial folds → systemic lupus erythematosus
qualifiers.shift: Sun-exposed distribution with sparing under the chin and in skin folds. A malar rash sparing the nasolabial folds suggests lupus.
qualifiers.misuse: Nasolabial sparing not checked, which is what separates lupus from rosacea and dermatomyositis

qualifiers.name: Dermatomal
qualifiers.established: Map the eruption against dermatomes and check midline respect
qualifiers.example: unilateral vesicular rash respecting the midline → herpes zoster
qualifiers.shift: A unilateral vesicular eruption respecting the midline within one dermatome is zoster and needs no confirmatory test to begin treatment.

qualifiers.name: Pruritic
qualifiers.established: Ask about itch and inspect for excoriation without primary lesions
qualifiers.example: generalized pruritus without rash → cholestasis or lymphoma
qualifiers.shift: Itch implies histamine or neural involvement. Generalized itch without primary rash raises cholestasis, uremia, iron deficiency, and lymphoma.

qualifiers.name: Nonpruritic
qualifiers.established: Ask specifically about itch
qualifiers.example: widespread nonpruritic eruption → secondary syphilis
qualifiers.shift: Absence of itch in a widespread rash is itself a clue, notably in secondary syphilis.

qualifiers.name: Nikolsky-positive
qualifiers.definition: Epidermis shears with lateral pressure on normal-appearing skin
qualifiers.established: Lateral shearing pressure on normal-appearing perilesional skin
qualifiers.example: positive Nikolsky sign with mucosal erosions → toxic epidermal necrolysis
qualifiers.shift: A dermatologic emergency sign indicating intraepidermal or dermoepidermal separation. With mucosal involvement and a recent new drug, treat as TEN and transfer to a burn unit.

qualifiers.name: Scaly
qualifiers.established: Inspection and gentle scraping
qualifiers.example: scaly plaque → psoriasis or dermatophyte infection
qualifiers.shift: Indicates epidermal involvement and abnormal keratinisation. Its presence or absence separates epidermal from purely dermal processes.

qualifiers.name: Silvery scale
qualifiers.definition: Thick micaceous white scale on a well-demarcated plaque
qualifiers.established: Inspection; removal may produce pinpoint bleeding
qualifiers.example: silvery scale on extensor plaques → plaque psoriasis
qualifiers.shift: With extensor distribution and sharp demarcation this is close to diagnostic of plaque psoriasis.

qualifiers.name: Lichenified
qualifiers.definition: Thickened skin with accentuated markings from chronic rubbing
qualifiers.established: Inspection for thickened skin with accentuated markings
qualifiers.example: lichenification → chronic atopic dermatitis
qualifiers.shift: Evidence of chronicity and of an itch-scratch cycle, which shifts management toward breaking that cycle.

qualifiers.name: Violaceous
qualifiers.established: Inspection in good light
qualifiers.example: violaceous periorbital rash with Gottron papules → dermatomyositis
qualifiers.shift: Violaceous periorbital change (heliotrope) with Gottron papules is close to specific for dermatomyositis and mandates a malignancy search in adults.
qualifiers.misuse: Missed in darker skin, where the violaceous hue is harder to appreciate

qualifiers.name: Well-demarcated
qualifiers.definition: Sharp border between involved and normal skin
qualifiers.established: Inspection and marking the border with a pen
qualifiers.example: sharply demarcated raised erythema → erysipelas
qualifiers.shift: Sharp raised borders in cellulitis suggest erysipelas and streptococcal etiology; indistinct borders suggest ordinary cellulitis.

qualifiers.name: Koebner phenomenon
qualifiers.definition: New lesions appearing at sites of trauma
qualifiers.established: Ask about lesions appearing at sites of injury
qualifiers.example: lesions along a scratch line → psoriasis or lichen planus
qualifiers.shift: A narrow differential and a useful confirmatory sign when the diagnosis is uncertain.

qualifiers.name: Satellite lesions
qualifiers.definition: Small discrete lesions surrounding a larger confluent area
qualifiers.established: Inspect the periphery of the main plaque
qualifiers.example: satellite pustules around an intertriginous rash → cutaneous candidiasis
qualifiers.shift: In an intertriginous rash, satellite pustules point to candida rather than simple intertrigo and change treatment to an antifungal.

qualifiers.name: Retiform purpura
qualifiers.established: Inspection for branching angulated geometry
qualifiers.associated: Vascular occlusion, calciphylaxis, DIC, cholesterol emboli
qualifiers.example: retiform purpura → calciphylaxis or vascular occlusion
qualifiers.shift: Its geometry reflects the branching pattern of an occluded vessel. Points to occlusion rather than inflammation, a different and often more urgent differential than palpable purpura.
qualifiers.misuse: Called palpable purpura, which points to inflammation rather than occlusion

qualifiers.name: Livedo racemosa
qualifiers.established: Inspection for asymmetric incomplete rings persisting on warming
qualifiers.example: irregular broken livedo → antiphospholipid syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Distinguished from benign physiologic livedo reticularis by its irregular, incomplete, and persistent pattern. Nearly always pathologic.
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with physiologic livedo reticularis, which is regular, symmetric, and reversible

qualifiers.name: Scarring alopecia
qualifiers.definition: Hair loss with loss of follicular ostia
qualifiers.established: Inspect the scalp with a dermatoscope for follicular openings
qualifiers.associated: Lichen planopilaris, discoid lupus, folliculitis decalvans
qualifiers.example: loss of follicular ostia → lichen planopilaris
qualifiers.shift: Irreversible and a trichologic emergency, since treatment can only prevent further loss. Absence of follicular openings is the bedside finding.
qualifiers.misuse: Not examined for ostia, so irreversible loss continues untreated

qualifiers.name: Nonscarring alopecia
qualifiers.definition: Hair loss with follicular openings preserved
qualifiers.established: Dermatoscopic inspection of the scalp
qualifiers.example: preserved follicular ostia → alopecia areata
qualifiers.shift: Potentially reversible and managed medically rather than urgently.

qualifiers.name: Umbilicated
qualifiers.established: Inspection with magnification
qualifiers.example: umbilicated papules in an immunocompromised patient → disseminated cryptococcosis
qualifiers.shift: Benign in a child with molluscum; in an immunocompromised adult, umbilicated papules can represent disseminated fungal infection and warrant biopsy.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed to be molluscum in an immunocompromised adult, where it may be disseminated fungal infection

qualifiers.name: Eschar
qualifiers.established: Full skin examination including axillae, groin, and scalp
qualifiers.associated: Rickettsial infection, anthrax, mucormycosis, ischemic necrosis
qualifiers.example: single necrotic eschar after travel → scrub typhus or tick-borne rickettsiosis
qualifiers.shift: In the right exposure history, a single eschar is close to diagnostic of scrub typhus or African tick bite fever. On the palate or turbinates it raises mucormycosis, a surgical emergency.
qualifiers.misuse: Not found because the whole skin is not examined

qualifiers.name: Nail pitting and onycholysis
qualifiers.definition: Small depressions in the nail plate, and nail separation
qualifiers.established: Inspect all twenty nails
qualifiers.example: nail pitting → psoriatic arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Nail involvement is closely associated with psoriatic arthritis, particularly distal interphalangeal disease, and can be the clue that reclassifies an arthritis.
qualifiers.misuse: Nails not examined in a patient with undifferentiated arthritis

qualifiers.name: Herald patch
qualifiers.definition: A single larger plaque preceding a wider eruption
qualifiers.established: History of a single preceding plaque plus distribution along skin lines
qualifiers.example: herald patch then a Christmas-tree eruption → pityriasis rosea
qualifiers.shift: With a subsequent Christmas-tree distribution along skin lines this is pityriasis rosea, self-limited and requiring no workup beyond excluding secondary syphilis.
qualifiers.misuse: Secondary syphilis not excluded, which it can closely mimic

qualifiers.name: Ecchymotic
qualifiers.established: Inspection and diascopy; nonblanching by definition
qualifiers.example: spontaneous ecchymoses → coagulopathy
qualifiers.shift: Larger than purpura and usually deeper. Spontaneous or minimally provoked ecchymoses raise a coagulation defect rather than a platelet or vessel problem
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to trauma in the elderly without considering anticoagulation or liver disease

qualifiers.name: Serpiginous
qualifiers.established: Inspection of the lesion border, often with serial marking
qualifiers.associated: Cutaneous larva migrans, some fungal and granulomatous lesions
qualifiers.example: serpiginous migrating track after beach exposure → cutaneous larva migrans
qualifiers.shift: A migrating track is close to specific for a burrowing organism. Marking the border and re-examining confirms migration

qualifiers.name: Discrete
qualifiers.established: Inspection for whether lesions merge
qualifiers.example: discrete vesicles at different stages → varicella
qualifiers.shift: Contrasts with confluent. Lesions in several stages of evolution simultaneously is characteristic of varicella

qualifiers.name: Regular
qualifiers.established: Pulse palpation and rhythm strip
qualifiers.associated: Sinus rhythm, SVT, atrial flutter with fixed block
qualifiers.example: regular narrow-complex tachycardia → AV nodal reentrant tachycardia
qualifiers.shift: Favors a single organized reentrant or automatic focus over fibrillation.

qualifiers.name: Irregularly irregular
qualifiers.established: Palpate for at least thirty seconds, then confirm on ECG
qualifiers.example: irregularly irregular pulse → atrial fibrillation
qualifiers.shift: Essentially diagnostic of AF at the bedside, and immediately raises stroke risk assessment and anticoagulation.
qualifiers.misuse: Confirmed by pulse alone; frequent ectopy mimics it

qualifiers.name: Regularly irregular
qualifiers.established: Rhythm strip showing a repeating pattern
qualifiers.example: regularly irregular pulse → ventricular bigeminy
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes patterned conduction disease and ectopy from fibrillation, a different differential and different management.

qualifiers.name: Narrow-complex
qualifiers.established: QRS duration on a 12-lead ECG
qualifiers.example: narrow-complex tachycardia → supraventricular tachycardia
qualifiers.shift: Conduction is traveling down the normal His-Purkinje system, so the rhythm originates at or above the AV node. Generally more benign and often adenosine-responsive.

qualifiers.name: Wide-complex
qualifiers.established: QRS duration of 120 ms or more on a 12-lead ECG
qualifiers.associated: VT, SVT with aberrancy, preexcitation, hyperkalemia
qualifiers.example: wide-complex tachycardia → ventricular tachycardia
qualifiers.shift: Ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise, particularly with structural heart disease. Treat as VT; do not give a calcium channel blocker.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as SVT with aberrancy in a patient with structural heart disease, where VT is far likelier

qualifiers.name: Monomorphic
qualifiers.established: QRS morphology consistent across beats
qualifiers.example: monomorphic ventricular tachycardia → scar-related reentry
qualifiers.shift: Implies a fixed anatomic reentry circuit, usually around prior infarct scar.

qualifiers.name: Polymorphic
qualifiers.established: Changing QRS morphology plus the baseline QT interval
qualifiers.example: polymorphic ventricular tachycardia → long QT with torsades
qualifiers.shift: Redirects toward acute ischemia or QT prolongation. Torsades needs magnesium and QT review, not standard antiarrhythmics.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with standard antiarrhythmics; torsades needs magnesium and QT review

qualifiers.name: Systolic
qualifiers.established: Auscultation timed against the carotid pulse
qualifiers.example: systolic ejection murmur → aortic stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Broad category including benign flow murmurs. Requires further qualifiers (timing, shape, radiation) to be useful.
qualifiers.misuse: Timed against the apex beat, which is unreliable in tachycardia

qualifiers.name: Diastolic
qualifiers.established: Auscultation with the patient sitting forward in expiration
qualifiers.example: early diastolic decrescendo murmur → aortic regurgitation
qualifiers.shift: Diastolic murmurs are essentially never benign. Their presence alone justifies echocardiography.

qualifiers.name: Holosystolic
qualifiers.established: Auscultation across the full systolic interval
qualifiers.example: holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla → mitral regurgitation
qualifiers.shift: Implies a pressure gradient present throughout systole, meaning a regurgitant or shunt lesion rather than an ejection lesion.

qualifiers.name: Crescendo-decrescendo
qualifiers.established: Auscultation for shape plus radiation
qualifiers.example: crescendo-decrescendo murmur radiating to the carotids → aortic stenosis
qualifiers.shift: An ejection pattern. Radiation to the carotids with a delayed weak pulse suggests severe AS; increase with Valsalva suggests HCM.

qualifiers.name: Low-pitched
qualifiers.definition: Lower frequency, heard with the bell
qualifiers.established: Bell at the apex, patient in the left lateral position
qualifiers.example: low-pitched apical diastolic rumble → mitral stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Low-frequency sounds imply high-volume low-velocity flow, heard best with the bell at the apex.
qualifiers.misuse: Auscultated with the diaphragm, which filters out the low frequencies

qualifiers.name: Pulsatile
qualifiers.definition: Expansile and synchronous with the pulse
qualifiers.established: Palpate for lateral expansion, not just transmitted pulsation
qualifiers.example: expansile pulsatile abdominal mass → abdominal aortic aneurysm
qualifiers.shift: An expansile pulsatile abdominal mass is an aortic aneurysm until imaged, and if painful, an emergency.

qualifiers.name: Compensated
qualifiers.established: Absence of ascites, encephalopathy, jaundice, or variceal bleeding
qualifiers.example: compensated cirrhosis → preserved synthetic function
qualifiers.shift: Defines the prognostic category and often the entire management approach.

qualifiers.name: Decompensated
qualifiers.established: Presence of a defining decompensating event
qualifiers.associated: Acute heart failure, cirrhosis with ascites
qualifiers.example: decompensated cirrhosis → spontaneous bacterial peritonitis as precipitant
qualifiers.shift: Always ask what precipitated it. Decompensation of a chronic disease usually has an identifiable trigger: infection, bleed, ischemia, arrhythmia, or nonadherence.
qualifiers.misuse: Precipitant not sought; decompensation almost always has a trigger

qualifiers.name: Fixed splitting of S2
qualifiers.definition: Split persists unchanged through the respiratory cycle
qualifiers.established: Auscultate at the left upper sternal border through the respiratory cycle
qualifiers.example: fixed splitting of S2 → atrial septal defect
qualifiers.shift: Close to specific for ASD, because the shunt equalises right and left filling across the respiratory cycle. Normal splitting widens on inspiration.
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed without watching respiration, so fixed and physiologic splitting cannot be distinguished

qualifiers.name: Pulsus paradoxus
qualifiers.definition: Inspiratory fall in systolic pressure greater than 10 mmHg
qualifiers.established: Deflate the cuff slowly and note the gap between first and all-beat Korotkoff sounds
qualifiers.example: pulsus paradoxus over 10 mmHg → cardiac tamponade
qualifiers.shift: An exaggeration of a normal phenomenon reflecting ventricular interdependence. With elevated JVP and muffled sounds it supports tamponade and argues for urgent echocardiography.
qualifiers.misuse: Estimated from the pulse oximetry waveform rather than measured

qualifiers.name: Pulsus parvus et tardus
qualifiers.definition: Weak and slowly rising carotid upstroke
qualifiers.established: Palpate the carotid, not the radial, pulse
qualifiers.example: slow-rising low-amplitude carotid upstroke → severe aortic stenosis
qualifiers.shift: One of the more reliable bedside indicators of severe AS, and it persists when the murmur softens as stroke volume falls.
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed at the radial artery, where the waveform is altered

qualifiers.name: Bounding or water-hammer
qualifiers.definition: Rapid rise and rapid collapse of the pulse
qualifiers.established: Palpate with the arm elevated
qualifiers.example: collapsing pulse with wide pulse pressure → aortic regurgitation
qualifiers.shift: A wide pulse pressure with collapsing quality points to aortic regurgitation or a high-output state such as thyrotoxicosis, anemia, or arteriovenous fistula.

qualifiers.name: Friction rub
qualifiers.definition: Scratchy triphasic sound unrelated to a valve
qualifiers.established: Auscultate at the left sternal border, patient leaning forward, in expiration
qualifiers.example: pericardial friction rub → acute pericarditis
qualifiers.shift: Highly specific for pericarditis but intermittent, so a single absent examination proves little. Listen repeatedly with the patient leaning forward.
qualifiers.misuse: Intermittent; a single negative examination proves nothing

qualifiers.name: Elevated JVP
qualifiers.definition: Jugular venous pressure raised above normal
qualifiers.established: Patient at 45 degrees, measure vertical height above the sternal angle
qualifiers.example: elevated JVP with clear lungs → right heart failure or tamponade
qualifiers.shift: The most useful bedside measure of volume status and right-sided filling. Separates cardiogenic from non-cardiogenic causes of dyspnea and of edema.
qualifiers.misuse: Measured against the wrong landmark or in the wrong position, making it uninterpretable

qualifiers.name: Displaced and sustained apex
qualifiers.definition: Apex beat lateral and inferior, with prolonged outward motion
qualifiers.established: Palpate in the left lateral position and localize against rib spaces
qualifiers.example: displaced sustained apex → left ventricular dilatation and pressure overload
qualifiers.shift: Displacement suggests dilatation; a sustained heaving quality suggests pressure overload from aortic stenosis or hypertension.

qualifiers.name: Kussmaul sign
qualifiers.definition: JVP rises rather than falls with inspiration
qualifiers.established: Observe the JVP through several respiratory cycles
qualifiers.associated: Constrictive pericarditis, RV infarction, restrictive cardiomyopathy
qualifiers.example: JVP rising on inspiration → constrictive pericarditis
qualifiers.shift: A paradoxical response indicating the right heart cannot accommodate increased venous return. Absent in tamponade, which is a useful discriminator between tamponade and constriction.

qualifiers.name: Prominent v waves
qualifiers.definition: Large systolic waves in the jugular venous waveform
qualifiers.established: Inspect the venous waveform timed against the carotid
qualifiers.example: prominent v waves with a pulsatile liver → severe tricuspid regurgitation
qualifiers.shift: Regurgitant flow into the atrium during systole. With a pulsatile liver, strongly supports severe tricuspid regurgitation.

qualifiers.name: Cannon a waves
qualifiers.established: Observe the neck for irregular large pulsations
qualifiers.associated: Complete heart block, VT, junctional rhythm
qualifiers.example: intermittent cannon a waves → complete heart block or ventricular tachycardia
qualifiers.shift: Indicates atrial contraction against a closed tricuspid valve, meaning AV dissociation. At the bedside this supports VT over SVT with aberrancy.

qualifiers.name: Pulsus alternans
qualifiers.definition: Alternating strong and weak beats with regular rhythm
qualifiers.established: Palpation, or an arterial line waveform
qualifiers.example: alternating pulse amplitude → severe left ventricular dysfunction
qualifiers.shift: Beat-to-beat variation in contractility indicating advanced systolic failure, and a poor prognostic sign.

qualifiers.name: Opening snap
qualifiers.definition: Early diastolic high-pitched sound after S2
qualifiers.established: Auscultate for the S2-to-snap interval
qualifiers.example: opening snap after S2 → mitral stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Indicates pliable leaflets, which matters for valvuloplasty candidacy. A shorter S2-to-snap interval indicates more severe stenosis.

qualifiers.name: S3 gallop
qualifiers.established: Bell at the apex, left lateral position
qualifiers.example: S3 gallop → systolic heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Rapid early filling into a compliant dilated ventricle. In an adult with dyspnea it substantially raises the likelihood of heart failure and is quite specific.

qualifiers.name: S4 gallop
qualifiers.definition: Low-pitched late diastolic sound before S1
qualifiers.established: Bell at the apex in late diastole
qualifiers.example: S4 gallop → left ventricular hypertrophy
qualifiers.shift: Atrial contraction against a stiff ventricle. Implies diastolic dysfunction and cannot occur in atrial fibrillation, since it requires organized atrial contraction.
qualifiers.misuse: Reported in atrial fibrillation, where it cannot occur

qualifiers.name: Pericardial knock
qualifiers.definition: Early diastolic sound from abrupt cessation of filling
qualifiers.established: Auscultation timed in early diastole
qualifiers.example: early diastolic knock → constrictive pericarditis
qualifiers.shift: Filling halted by the rigid pericardium. Supports constriction over restrictive cardiomyopathy.

qualifiers.name: Increases with Valsalva
qualifiers.established: Auscultate at baseline and during strain
qualifiers.example: murmur louder with Valsalva → hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
qualifiers.shift: Nearly all murmurs soften with reduced preload. The two that get louder are dynamic outflow obstruction and prolapse, so this maneuver is close to diagnostic.
qualifiers.misuse: Maneuvers not performed, so a dynamic murmur is called aortic stenosis

qualifiers.name: Increases with handgrip
qualifiers.established: Auscultate during sustained isometric handgrip
qualifiers.example: murmur louder with handgrip → mitral regurgitation
qualifiers.shift: Increased systemic resistance augments regurgitant and shunt flow while reducing aortic stenosis and HCM murmurs, separating regurgitant from ejection lesions.

qualifiers.name: Electrical alternans
qualifiers.established: 12-lead ECG examined for beat-to-beat amplitude variation
qualifiers.example: electrical alternans with tachycardia → large pericardial effusion
qualifiers.shift: Reflects the heart swinging within a large effusion. With sinus tachycardia and low voltage it is highly suggestive of tamponade.

qualifiers.name: Concordant ST elevation
qualifiers.definition: ST elevation in the same direction as the QRS
qualifiers.established: Apply Sgarbossa criteria to the 12-lead ECG
qualifiers.associated: STEMI in left bundle branch block or paced rhythm
qualifiers.example: concordant ST elevation in LBBB → acute myocardial infarction
qualifiers.shift: The most specific Sgarbossa criterion. Allows infarct diagnosis despite a bundle branch block that would otherwise obscure it.
qualifiers.misuse: ECG dismissed as uninterpretable because of the bundle branch block

qualifiers.name: Reciprocal changes
qualifiers.definition: ST depression in leads opposite the infarct territory
qualifiers.established: Examine leads opposite the territory of elevation
qualifiers.example: ST elevation with reciprocal depression → STEMI
qualifiers.shift: Substantially increases specificity for infarction over pericarditis and early repolarization, both of which lack true reciprocal change.

qualifiers.name: Delta wave
qualifiers.established: 12-lead ECG examined for a slurred QRS upstroke
qualifiers.example: short PR with a delta wave → Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Indicates an accessory pathway. Changes management of atrial fibrillation dramatically, since AV nodal blockers can accelerate conduction down the pathway.
qualifiers.misuse: Missed before giving AV nodal blockers for atrial fibrillation, which can be fatal

qualifiers.name: Low voltage
qualifiers.established: QRS amplitude criteria on ECG, compared against echocardiographic wall thickness
qualifiers.example: low voltage with thick walls on echo → cardiac amyloidosis
qualifiers.shift: Low voltage with echocardiographic wall thickening is a classic mismatch suggesting cardiac amyloidosis rather than hypertrophy.
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to obesity or COPD without comparing against the echo

qualifiers.name: Fixed perfusion defect
qualifiers.definition: Reduced uptake on both stress and rest imaging
qualifiers.established: Stress and rest myocardial perfusion imaging
qualifiers.example: fixed inferior perfusion defect → prior myocardial infarction
qualifiers.shift: Scar rather than ischemia. Predicts no benefit from revascularization in that territory.

qualifiers.name: Reversible perfusion defect
qualifiers.definition: Reduced uptake on stress that normalizes at rest
qualifiers.established: Stress and rest myocardial perfusion imaging
qualifiers.example: large reversible anterior defect → inducible ischemia in the LAD territory
qualifiers.shift: Viable but ischemic myocardium. This is the finding that supports revascularization, and its extent guides how strongly.

qualifiers.name: Hibernating myocardium
qualifiers.definition: Chronically underperfused but viable, with impaired function
qualifiers.established: Viability imaging with PET, MRI, or low-dose dobutamine echo
qualifiers.example: hibernating myocardium → recoverable dysfunction after revascularization
qualifiers.shift: Dysfunction that can recover after revascularization, which is why viability assessment can change a decision from medical therapy to intervention.
qualifiers.misuse: Not assessed, so revascularizable dysfunction is written off as fixed cardiomyopathy

qualifiers.name: Stunned myocardium
qualifiers.definition: Transient dysfunction after a reperfused ischemic insult
qualifiers.established: Serial imaging demonstrating recovery over days to weeks
qualifiers.example: stunned myocardium → takotsubo or post-arrest dysfunction
qualifiers.shift: Predicts spontaneous recovery over days to weeks and argues against premature decisions about devices or transplant.
qualifiers.misuse: Permanent device decisions made before recovery has had time to occur

qualifiers.name: Regional wall motion abnormality
qualifiers.definition: Impaired contraction confined to a coronary territory
qualifiers.established: Echocardiography assessing segments against coronary territories
qualifiers.example: regional wall motion abnormality → coronary territory infarction
qualifiers.shift: A territorial pattern implies coronary disease, whereas global hypokinesis suggests a diffuse insult such as myocarditis, toxin, or tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.

qualifiers.name: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
qualifiers.definition: Systolic dysfunction attributable to coronary disease
qualifiers.established: Coronary angiography or CT angiography
qualifiers.example: ischemic cardiomyopathy → multivessel coronary disease
qualifiers.shift: Determines whether revascularization is part of heart failure therapy. Usually requires angiography or CT to establish rather than assume.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed from risk factors alone without imaging the coronaries

qualifiers.name: Tachycardic
qualifiers.definition: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute
qualifiers.established: Pulse or monitored rate, confirmed against the ECG
qualifiers.associated: Sepsis, hypovolemia, pain, PE, arrhythmia, thyrotoxicosis
qualifiers.example: persistent tachycardia after adequate resuscitation → pulmonary embolism or ongoing bleeding
qualifiers.shift: A nonspecific but sensitive marker of physiologic stress. Its persistence after the obvious cause is treated is the informative part
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to pain or anxiety, which is the commonest way early shock and PE are missed

qualifiers.name: Bradycardic
qualifiers.definition: Heart rate below 60 beats per minute
qualifiers.established: Pulse and ECG, with a medication review
qualifiers.associated: AV block, medications, hypothyroidism, raised intracranial pressure, athletic conditioning
qualifiers.example: bradycardia with hypotension → complete heart block
qualifiers.shift: Whether it is symptomatic determines management. Bradycardia with hypertension and irregular breathing suggests raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as pathologic in trained athletes, where resting bradycardia is normal

qualifiers.name: Nonpulsatile
qualifiers.definition: Not synchronized with the arterial pulse
qualifiers.established: Palpation with attention to expansile versus transmitted movement
qualifiers.example: nonpulsatile abdominal mass → tumor rather than aneurysm
qualifiers.shift: Argues against a vascular lesion. Note that a mass overlying the aorta can transmit pulsation without being expansile
qualifiers.misuse: Transmitted pulsation mistaken for an expansile one, which is the distinction that matters for aneurysm

qualifiers.name: Productive
qualifiers.established: Ask about volume, color, and daily pattern
qualifiers.example: large-volume daily purulent sputum → bronchiectasis
qualifiers.shift: Suggests airway or alveolar secretions. Chronic daily large-volume purulent sputum suggests bronchiectasis.

qualifiers.name: Nonproductive
qualifiers.established: History plus a medication review
qualifiers.associated: ILD, ACE inhibitor cough, viral infection, heart failure
qualifiers.example: chronic dry cough → ACE inhibitor cough or interstitial lung disease
qualifiers.shift: Shifts toward interstitial, cardiac, drug-related, and postinfectious causes. Always check the medication list for an ACE inhibitor.
qualifiers.misuse: Medication list not reviewed; ACE inhibitor cough can begin months after starting

qualifiers.name: Blood-streaked
qualifiers.definition: Small amount of blood in sputum
qualifiers.established: Direct questioning and inspection of sputum
qualifiers.example: blood-streaked sputum in a smoker → bronchogenic carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Even minor hemoptysis in a smoker over 40 requires imaging and usually bronchoscopy.
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to bronchitis in a smoker over 40 without imaging

qualifiers.name: Massive hemoptysis
qualifiers.established: Estimate volume over 24 hours
qualifiers.example: massive hemoptysis → bronchiectasis or cavitary tuberculosis
qualifiers.shift: The threat is asphyxiation, not exsanguination. Position bleeding side down and call for bronchoscopy or embolization.
qualifiers.misuse: Managed as a bleeding problem; the threat is asphyxiation

qualifiers.name: Inspiratory
qualifiers.established: Listen over the neck during quiet breathing
qualifiers.example: inspiratory stridor → extrathoracic airway obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Localizes above the thoracic inlet: larynx, vocal cords, upper trachea. An airway emergency until characterized.
qualifiers.misuse: Mistaken for wheeze and treated with bronchodilators

qualifiers.name: Expiratory
qualifiers.established: Auscultation during forced expiration
qualifiers.example: expiratory polyphonic wheeze → asthma
qualifiers.shift: Intrathoracic airway narrowing that worsens as pleural pressure rises during exhalation.

qualifiers.name: Biphasic
qualifiers.established: Listen through both respiratory phases
qualifiers.example: biphasic stridor → fixed subglottic stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Implies a fixed lesion at the thoracic inlet that does not vary with the respiratory cycle.

qualifiers.name: Monophonic
qualifiers.established: Auscultate for a single constant pitch at one location
qualifiers.example: fixed monophonic wheeze → endobronchial tumor or foreign body
qualifiers.shift: A single fixed pitch implies one large airway. Not asthma. Warrants imaging and bronchoscopy.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as asthma; a fixed monophonic wheeze needs imaging and bronchoscopy

qualifiers.name: Polyphonic
qualifiers.established: Auscultation for multiple simultaneous pitches
qualifiers.example: polyphonic wheeze → asthma or COPD
qualifiers.shift: Diffuse small airway disease, the expected finding in asthma and COPD.

qualifiers.name: Hypoxemic
qualifiers.established: Arterial blood gas with PaO2 and the A-a gradient
qualifiers.example: hypoxemic respiratory failure → pneumonia or ARDS
qualifiers.shift: Type 1 failure, an oxygenation problem. Points to shunt or V/Q mismatch and directs toward the lung parenchyma or vasculature.

qualifiers.name: Hypercapnic
qualifiers.established: Arterial or venous blood gas with PaCO2 and pH
qualifiers.associated: COPD, obesity hypoventilation, neuromuscular disease, opioids
qualifiers.example: hypercapnic respiratory failure → COPD or opioid-induced hypoventilation
qualifiers.shift: Type 2 failure, a ventilation problem. Points to the pump: drive, chest wall, or respiratory muscles. Changes the intervention to ventilatory support rather than oxygen alone.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed from oximetry, which cannot detect hypercapnia

qualifiers.name: Obstructive
qualifiers.established: Spirometry before and after bronchodilator
qualifiers.example: reduced FEV1/FVC ratio → COPD
qualifiers.shift: Directs to the airways.

qualifiers.name: Restrictive
qualifiers.definition: Reduced lung volumes with preserved ratio
qualifiers.established: Full pulmonary function tests with lung volumes and DLCO
qualifiers.associated: ILD, obesity, neuromuscular disease, chest wall disease
qualifiers.example: reduced total lung capacity → interstitial lung disease
qualifiers.shift: Directs to parenchyma, chest wall, or neuromuscular pump. DLCO then separates parenchymal disease (reduced) from extraparenchymal causes (preserved).
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed from spirometry alone, which cannot establish restriction

qualifiers.name: Reversible
qualifiers.established: Post-bronchodilator spirometry meeting reversibility criteria
qualifiers.example: bronchodilator-reversible obstruction → asthma
qualifiers.shift: Bronchodilator responsiveness supports asthma over fixed COPD and predicts benefit from inhaled therapy.

qualifiers.name: Consolidative
qualifiers.established: Chest radiograph or CT
qualifiers.example: consolidation with air bronchograms → lobar pneumonia
qualifiers.shift: Air bronchograms indicate the airways remain patent while the alveoli are filled. Favors infection, though blood, pus, cells, and water all consolidate.

qualifiers.name: Ground-glass
qualifiers.definition: Hazy opacity that does not obscure vessels
qualifiers.established: CT chest
qualifiers.example: ground-glass opacities → viral pneumonia or pulmonary edema
qualifiers.shift: Partial alveolar filling or interstitial thickening. Broad, but combined with distribution it becomes powerful.

qualifiers.name: Cavitary
qualifiers.definition: Contains a gas-filled space with a wall
qualifiers.established: CT chest, with attention to wall thickness and location
qualifiers.associated: TB, abscess, septic emboli, squamous carcinoma
qualifiers.example: upper lobe cavitation → reactivation tuberculosis
qualifiers.shift: Sharply narrows the differential. Upper lobe cavitation suggests TB; multiple peripheral cavities suggest septic emboli.

qualifiers.name: Nodular
qualifiers.established: CT chest with attention to nodule distribution
qualifiers.example: perilymphatic nodules → sarcoidosis
qualifiers.shift: Distribution is decisive: perilymphatic suggests sarcoidosis, centrilobular suggests airway disease, random suggests hematogenous spread.
qualifiers.misuse: Distribution not characterized, which is where the diagnostic information lies

qualifiers.name: Spiculated
qualifiers.established: CT chest with thin sections
qualifiers.example: spiculated pulmonary nodule → primary lung carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Spiculation reflects desmoplastic reaction and is among the strongest morphologic predictors of malignancy.

qualifiers.name: Calcified
qualifiers.established: CT chest assessing the calcification pattern
qualifiers.example: centrally calcified nodule → healed granuloma
qualifiers.shift: Benign patterns (central, laminated, diffuse, popcorn) are reassuring; eccentric or stippled calcification is not.

qualifiers.name: Apical
qualifiers.established: CT chest with zonal assessment
qualifiers.example: apical fibrocavitary change → tuberculosis or silicosis
qualifiers.shift: Upper lobe predominance narrows considerably, driven by regional oxygen tension and lymphatic clearance.

qualifiers.name: Basilar
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.example: basilar subpleural reticulation → idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
qualifiers.shift: Basilar and peripheral reticulation with traction bronchiectasis is the usual interstitial pneumonia pattern of IPF.

qualifiers.name: Peripheral-predominant
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.example: peripheral consolidation with subpleural sparing → organizing pneumonia
qualifiers.shift: Subpleural sparing or peripheral banding is characteristic of organizing pneumonia.

qualifiers.name: Dependent
qualifiers.established: Compare supine and prone imaging where feasible
qualifiers.example: dependent posterior opacities → atelectasis
qualifiers.shift: Often positional and reversible. Distinguishing dependent atelectasis from true disease avoids unnecessary treatment.
qualifiers.misuse: Read as disease when it is positional and reversible

qualifiers.name: Exudative
qualifiers.established: Thoracentesis with Light criteria on paired fluid and serum
qualifiers.example: exudative pleural effusion → parapneumonic effusion or malignancy
qualifiers.shift: Meeting any Light criterion makes it an exudate and mandates a search for local pleural pathology: infection, cancer, or infarction.

qualifiers.name: Transudative
qualifiers.established: Thoracentesis with Light criteria; check the albumin gradient if diuresed
qualifiers.example: transudative effusion → heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Systemic hydrostatic or oncotic imbalance. Treat the underlying organ failure rather than the pleural space.
qualifiers.misuse: Light criteria overcall exudates in diuresed patients; use the serum-to-pleural albumin gradient

qualifiers.name: Loculated
qualifiers.established: Ultrasound of the pleural space for septations
qualifiers.example: loculated effusion → empyema
qualifiers.shift: Loculation predicts failure of simple drainage and raises the need for fibrinolytics or surgical decortication.
qualifiers.misuse: Chest radiograph alone cannot detect loculation

qualifiers.name: Fine crackles
qualifiers.established: Auscultate the bases at end-inspiration
qualifiers.example: fine late-inspiratory Velcro crackles → pulmonary fibrosis
qualifiers.shift: Late-inspiratory Velcro crackles at the bases are among the earliest signs of pulmonary fibrosis, often preceding symptoms and imaging changes.

qualifiers.name: Coarse crackles
qualifiers.definition: Lower-pitched, early-inspiratory, may clear with cough
qualifiers.established: Auscultate before and after a cough
qualifiers.example: coarse crackles clearing with cough → retained secretions
qualifiers.shift: Clearance with coughing suggests airway secretions rather than parenchymal disease, and argues against fibrosis.
qualifiers.misuse: Not reassessed after coughing, so secretions are mistaken for parenchymal disease

qualifiers.name: Bronchial breath sounds
qualifiers.definition: Loud tubular sounds heard over lung fields
qualifiers.established: Auscultation comparing with the contralateral side
qualifiers.example: bronchial breath sounds over a lung field → consolidation
qualifiers.shift: Consolidated lung conducts sound better than air-filled lung. With egophony and dullness this triad indicates consolidation rather than effusion.

qualifiers.name: Egophony
qualifiers.definition: Spoken E heard as A on auscultation
qualifiers.established: Ask the patient to say E while auscultating
qualifiers.example: E-to-A change → consolidation
qualifiers.shift: A selective transmission change through consolidated lung. Simple, specific, and largely forgotten.

qualifiers.name: Dull to percussion
qualifiers.established: Percussion combined with fremitus and auscultation
qualifiers.example: dullness with absent breath sounds and fremitus → pleural effusion
qualifiers.shift: With decreased breath sounds and absent fremitus, favors effusion. With increased fremitus and bronchial sounds, favors consolidation. The combination discriminates; the percussion note alone does not.
qualifiers.misuse: Percussion note interpreted alone, which cannot separate effusion from consolidation

qualifiers.name: Hyperresonant
qualifiers.established: Percussion and auscultation, comparing sides
qualifiers.example: hyperresonance with absent breath sounds → tension pneumothorax
qualifiers.shift: With absent breath sounds and tracheal deviation this is a tension pneumothorax and should be decompressed before imaging.
qualifiers.misuse: Confirmed by imaging first; tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis needing immediate decompression

qualifiers.name: Tree-in-bud
qualifiers.definition: Centrilobular branching nodular opacities on CT
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.associated: Endobronchial spread of TB, MAC, aspiration, bronchiolitis
qualifiers.example: tree-in-bud opacities → endobronchial spread of tuberculosis
qualifiers.shift: Indicates small airway filling with mucus, pus, or inflammatory material. Strongly favors infectious bronchiolitis and endobronchial spread over interstitial disease.

qualifiers.name: Honeycombing
qualifiers.definition: Clustered subpleural cystic airspaces with defined walls
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT with thin sections
qualifiers.example: subpleural honeycombing → usual interstitial pneumonia
qualifiers.shift: Represents established, irreversible architectural destruction. With basal subpleural reticulation and traction bronchiectasis it defines the usual interstitial pneumonia pattern and can establish IPF without biopsy.
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with traction bronchiectasis or emphysema, which changes the pattern classification

qualifiers.name: Traction bronchiectasis
qualifiers.definition: Airway dilatation caused by surrounding fibrotic retraction
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.example: traction bronchiectasis → established fibrosis
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes fibrosis from reversible ground-glass. Its presence means scarring rather than active alveolitis, which changes both prognosis and the expected benefit from immunosuppression.

qualifiers.name: Crazy paving
qualifiers.definition: Ground-glass with superimposed interlobular septal thickening
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.example: crazy paving → pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
qualifiers.shift: A short and specific differential; classically pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, but also seen in PJP and diffuse alveolar damage.

qualifiers.name: Widened A-a gradient
qualifiers.definition: Alveolar-arterial oxygen difference above predicted for age
qualifiers.established: Arterial blood gas with the alveolar gas equation, corrected for age
qualifiers.example: widened A-a gradient → intrinsic lung disease
qualifiers.shift: Separates intrinsic lung disease from hypoventilation. A normal gradient with hypoxemia points to hypoventilation or low inspired oxygen, an entirely different differential.
qualifiers.misuse: Not calculated, so hypoventilation and lung disease are not separated

qualifiers.name: Shunt physiology
qualifiers.definition: Hypoxemia that corrects poorly with supplemental oxygen
qualifiers.established: Observe the response to high inspired oxygen
qualifiers.example: hypoxemia not correcting on 100% oxygen → intrapulmonary shunt
qualifiers.shift: Blood bypasses ventilated alveoli entirely. Failure to correct on high inspired oxygen is the bedside test and directs toward recruitment strategies rather than more oxygen.

qualifiers.name: V/Q mismatch
qualifiers.definition: Hypoxemia that corrects readily with supplemental oxygen
qualifiers.established: Observe the response to modest supplemental oxygen
qualifiers.example: hypoxemia correcting readily with oxygen → V/Q mismatch
qualifiers.shift: The commonest mechanism of hypoxemia and the one most responsive to oxygen therapy.

qualifiers.name: Diffusion limitation
qualifiers.definition: Impaired transfer across the alveolar-capillary membrane
qualifiers.established: Full pulmonary function tests including DLCO corrected for hemoglobin
qualifiers.example: isolated low DLCO → pulmonary vascular disease
qualifiers.shift: An isolated low DLCO with normal spirometry and volumes raises pulmonary vascular disease, including chronic thromboembolic disease and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
qualifiers.misuse: Not corrected for hemoglobin, so anemia mimics diffusion impairment

qualifiers.name: Mosaic attenuation
qualifiers.definition: Patchwork of differing lung density on CT
qualifiers.established: Inspiratory and expiratory CT
qualifiers.associated: Small airway disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, ILD
qualifiers.example: mosaic attenuation → small airway disease or chronic thromboembolic disease
qualifiers.shift: Expiratory imaging distinguishes air trapping from vascular causes; if the dark regions become darker on expiration, the mechanism is small airway obstruction.

qualifiers.name: Air trapping
qualifiers.definition: Failure of lung regions to empty on expiration
qualifiers.established: Paired inspiratory and expiratory imaging
qualifiers.example: air trapping on expiratory CT → bronchiolitis
qualifiers.shift: Establishes small airway obstruction and can reveal disease invisible on inspiratory images alone.
qualifiers.misuse: Expiratory images not obtained, so the finding cannot be made

qualifiers.name: Upper-lobe predominant
qualifiers.definition: Disease concentrated in the upper zones
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT with zonal assessment
qualifiers.example: upper-lobe predominant fibrosis → hypersensitivity pneumonitis or sarcoidosis
qualifiers.shift: Zonal predominance is one of the most efficient discriminators in interstitial lung disease and immediately splits a long differential.

qualifiers.name: Subpleural sparing
qualifiers.definition: Immediate subpleural lung spared while deeper lung is involved
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT chest
qualifiers.example: subpleural sparing → nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
qualifiers.shift: Argues against usual interstitial pneumonia, which is characteristically subpleural, and supports NSIP, which has a different prognosis and greater steroid responsiveness.

qualifiers.name: Kerley B lines
qualifiers.established: Chest radiograph, peripheral lower zones
qualifiers.example: Kerley B lines → interstitial pulmonary edema
qualifiers.shift: Thickened interlobular septa. In acute dyspnea supports cardiogenic edema; when persistent and nodular, raises lymphangitic carcinomatosis.

qualifiers.name: Cephalization
qualifiers.established: Erect chest radiograph
qualifiers.example: upper zone vascular redistribution → raised left atrial pressure
qualifiers.shift: An early radiographic sign of raised left-sided filling pressures, appearing before frank edema.
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed on a supine film, where redistribution is a normal artifact

qualifiers.name: Silhouette sign
qualifiers.definition: Loss of a normal border between structures of differing density
qualifiers.established: Frontal chest radiograph
qualifiers.example: loss of the right heart border → right middle lobe consolidation
qualifiers.shift: Localizes disease anatomically on a plain film. Loss of the right heart border implies right middle lobe; loss of the left hemidiaphragm implies left lower lobe.

qualifiers.name: Air crescent sign
qualifiers.definition: Crescent of air separating a cavity wall from its contents
qualifiers.established: CT chest
qualifiers.example: air crescent → recovering angioinvasive aspergillosis
qualifiers.shift: In neutropenic patients it typically signals neutrophil recovery and retraction of infarcted lung, and it can herald hemoptysis.

qualifiers.name: Halo sign
qualifiers.established: CT chest in a neutropenic patient
qualifiers.example: ground-glass halo around a nodule → invasive aspergillosis
qualifiers.shift: Represents perilesional hemorrhage. In a neutropenic patient it is an early and actionable sign of invasive fungal infection.

qualifiers.name: Deep sulcus sign
qualifiers.definition: Abnormally deep lateral costophrenic angle on a supine film
qualifiers.established: Supine chest radiograph, examining the costophrenic angles
qualifiers.example: deep sulcus sign → pneumothorax in a supine patient
qualifiers.shift: Air collects anteriorly and basally when supine, so the classic apical lucency is absent. Prevents a missed pneumothorax on ICU films.
qualifiers.misuse: Apical lucency looked for on a supine film, where air collects anteriorly and basally

qualifiers.name: Auto-PEEP
qualifiers.definition: Incomplete exhalation leaving trapped positive pressure
qualifiers.established: End-expiratory hold maneuver on the ventilator
qualifiers.example: auto-PEEP with hypotension → dynamic hyperinflation
qualifiers.shift: A cause of hypotension and of apparent ventilator failure. Managed by reducing respiratory rate and prolonging expiratory time, which is counterintuitive in a hypercapnic patient.
qualifiers.misuse: Hypotension treated with fluid and vasopressors rather than by disconnecting and reducing the rate

qualifiers.name: Mucoid sputum
qualifiers.definition: Clear or white mucus without pus
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of expectorated sputum
qualifiers.example: mucoid sputum → noninfective airway secretion
qualifiers.shift: Mucus without purulence argues against bacterial infection and reduces the case for antibiotics in an exacerbation
qualifiers.misuse: Color used alone to decide on antibiotics; purulence correlates imperfectly with bacterial infection

qualifiers.name: Interstitial
qualifiers.definition: Involving the lung interstitium rather than airspaces
qualifiers.established: High-resolution CT, or a chest radiograph showing reticular rather than alveolar pattern
qualifiers.example: interstitial reticular pattern → interstitial lung disease
qualifiers.shift: Directs to the tissue between airspaces rather than the airspaces themselves. Distribution and the presence of fibrosis then narrow it further
qualifiers.misuse: Any hazy opacity called interstitial; airspace and interstitial patterns are radiologically distinct

qualifiers.name: Free-flowing
qualifiers.established: Lateral decubitus radiograph or ultrasound with repositioning
qualifiers.example: free-flowing effusion → transudate or simple parapneumonic effusion
qualifiers.shift: Predicts that simple drainage will work, and argues against empyema or an organizing process

qualifiers.name: Bloody
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of stool where possible
qualifiers.associated: IBD, invasive colitis, ischemic colitis, malignancy
qualifiers.example: bloody diarrhea → invasive colitis or inflammatory bowel disease
qualifiers.shift: Implies mucosal invasion or ulceration. Shifts from secretory and osmotic causes toward inflammatory, infectious-invasive, and ischemic disease.
qualifiers.misuse: Reported by the patient without inspection; beets and bismuth confuse both ends

qualifiers.name: Watery
qualifiers.established: Stool description plus volume estimate
qualifiers.example: large-volume watery diarrhea → secretory process or cholera
qualifiers.shift: Secretory or osmotic mechanism. A fasting trial separates the two: osmotic diarrhea stops, secretory does not.

qualifiers.name: Mucoid
qualifiers.established: History and inspection
qualifiers.example: mucoid stool → inflammatory bowel disease
qualifiers.shift: Suggests mucosal irritation or inflammation.

qualifiers.name: Greasy or steatorrheic
qualifiers.definition: Excess fat in stool, floating and foul, hard to flush
qualifiers.established: Ask about floating, foul odor, and difficulty flushing
qualifiers.example: greasy floating stool → pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
qualifiers.shift: Fat malabsorption. Separates maldigestion (pancreatic exocrine insufficiency) from malabsorption (mucosal disease such as celiac).

qualifiers.name: Melena
qualifiers.established: Digital rectal examination and direct inspection
qualifiers.example: melena → upper gastrointestinal bleeding
qualifiers.shift: Implies bleeding proximal to the ligament of Treitz with time for hemoglobin degradation. Roughly 50 mL is enough. Prompts upper endoscopy.
qualifiers.misuse: Iron and bismuth produce black stool without bleeding; inspect and test rather than accept the report

qualifiers.name: Hematochezia
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus hemodynamic assessment
qualifiers.associated: Diverticular bleed, hemorrhoids, colitis, brisk upper bleed
qualifiers.example: hematochezia with instability → brisk upper gastrointestinal bleed
qualifiers.shift: Usually lower GI, but a brisk upper source can present this way; hematochezia with hemodynamic instability warrants upper endoscopy first.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed to be a lower source; brisk upper bleeding presents this way and needs upper endoscopy first

qualifiers.name: Bilious
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of the vomitus
qualifiers.example: bilious emesis in a neonate → malrotation with midgut volvulus
qualifiers.shift: In a neonate, bilious emesis is malrotation with volvulus until excluded, a surgical emergency.
qualifiers.misuse: Described by report rather than inspected

qualifiers.name: Nonbilious
qualifiers.established: Inspection of vomitus
qualifiers.example: nonbilious projectile emesis in an infant → pyloric stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Localizes the obstruction proximal to the ampulla of Vater.

qualifiers.name: Feculent
qualifiers.established: Inspection and smell of the vomitus or nasogastric output
qualifiers.associated: Distal small bowel obstruction, gastrocolic fistula
qualifiers.example: feculent emesis → distal small bowel obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Implies long-standing distal obstruction with bacterial overgrowth, or an enteric fistula.

qualifiers.name: Projectile
qualifiers.established: History of force and effortlessness
qualifiers.example: projectile vomiting with headache → raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.shift: In infants suggests gastric outlet obstruction; in adults with headache raises raised intracranial pressure.

qualifiers.name: Conjugated (direct)
qualifiers.established: Fractionated serum bilirubin
qualifiers.example: conjugated hyperbilirubinemia → biliary obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Always pathologic. Directs to hepatobiliary excretion or obstruction.
qualifiers.misuse: Total bilirubin ordered without fractionation, which discards the branch point

qualifiers.name: Unconjugated (indirect)
qualifiers.established: Fractionated bilirubin plus reticulocytes, LDH, haptoglobin
qualifiers.example: unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia → hemolysis or Gilbert syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Directs upstream to overproduction or impaired uptake and conjugation. Isolated mild unconjugated elevation with otherwise normal tests is usually Gilbert syndrome.

qualifiers.name: Cholestatic
qualifiers.established: Liver panel with the R factor calculated
qualifiers.example: disproportionate alkaline phosphatase rise → biliary obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Localizes toward bile ducts. Next step is imaging to separate intrahepatic from extrahepatic obstruction, then AMA if ducts are normal.
qualifiers.misuse: GGT not checked, so a bony source of alkaline phosphatase is not excluded

qualifiers.name: Hepatocellular
qualifiers.established: Liver panel with the R factor calculated
qualifiers.example: aminotransferases above 1000 → ischemic or toxic hepatitis
qualifiers.shift: Localizes to hepatocytes. Magnitude helps: values above 1000 suggest ischemia, acetaminophen, or acute viral hepatitis.

qualifiers.name: Prehepatic
qualifiers.established: Fractionated bilirubin plus a hemolysis screen
qualifiers.example: prehepatic jaundice → hemolytic anemia
qualifiers.shift: Sends you to the CBC, smear, reticulocyte count, LDH, and haptoglobin rather than to liver imaging.

qualifiers.name: Intrahepatic
qualifiers.established: Ultrasound showing nondilated ducts, then AMA testing
qualifiers.example: intrahepatic cholestasis → primary biliary cholangitis
qualifiers.shift: Ducts are not dilated on imaging. Moves toward serology, drug review, and biopsy.

qualifiers.name: Extrahepatic
qualifiers.definition: Outside the liver in the biliary tree
qualifiers.established: Ultrasound or MRCP showing duct dilation
qualifiers.example: extrahepatic obstruction → choledocholithiasis or pancreatic head tumor
qualifiers.shift: Dilated ducts. Moves toward ERCP or surgical decompression, and painless obstruction raises malignancy.

qualifiers.name: High SAAG
qualifiers.definition: Serum-ascites albumin gradient of 1.1 g/dL or more
qualifiers.established: Paired serum and ascitic albumin on the same day
qualifiers.example: high SAAG ascites → portal hypertension from cirrhosis
qualifiers.shift: Establishes portal hypertension as the mechanism and largely excludes peritoneal disease. More reliable than ascitic protein or older exudate-transudate schemes.
qualifiers.misuse: Ascitic protein used instead, which is far less reliable

qualifiers.name: Low SAAG
qualifiers.established: Paired serum and ascitic albumin
qualifiers.associated: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, TB peritonitis, pancreatic ascites
qualifiers.example: low SAAG ascites → peritoneal carcinomatosis
qualifiers.shift: Redirects to the peritoneum itself and prompts cytology, adenosine deaminase, and imaging for peritoneal disease.

qualifiers.name: Shifting dullness
qualifiers.established: Percuss the flank, roll the patient, and re-percuss
qualifiers.example: shifting dullness → free ascites
qualifiers.shift: Indicates free rather than loculated fluid, and generally requires a moderate volume before it is detectable.
qualifiers.misuse: Requires a moderate volume; absence does not exclude ascites

qualifiers.name: Tympanitic
qualifiers.definition: Drum-like percussion note over the abdomen
qualifiers.established: Percussion across all quadrants
qualifiers.example: distended tympanitic abdomen → bowel obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Indicates gas-filled bowel. With absent bowel sounds it suggests ileus; with high-pitched rushes it suggests mechanical obstruction.

qualifiers.name: High-pitched bowel sounds
qualifiers.established: Auscultate for at least a minute in one location
qualifiers.example: high-pitched tinkling bowel sounds → mechanical obstruction
qualifiers.shift: Bowel straining against a mechanical blockage. Progression to silence suggests exhaustion, ischemia, or perforation and is a worsening sign.
qualifiers.misuse: Progression to silence is a worsening sign that goes unnoticed if not reassessed

qualifiers.name: Reducible
qualifiers.definition: A hernia that can be returned to the abdomen
qualifiers.established: Gentle manual reduction with the patient supine
qualifiers.example: reducible groin hernia → uncomplicated inguinal hernia
qualifiers.shift: Reassuring; elective repair.

qualifiers.name: Incarcerated
qualifiers.definition: Trapped, not reducible, but still perfused
qualifiers.established: Attempted reduction plus assessment of tenderness and overlying skin
qualifiers.example: irreducible tender hernia → incarcerated hernia
qualifiers.shift: Urgent, because obstruction and progression to strangulation may follow.

qualifiers.name: Strangulated
qualifiers.established: Systemic toxicity, severe pain, and skin change over an irreducible hernia
qualifiers.example: strangulated hernia → ischemic bowel
qualifiers.shift: A surgical emergency. Pain out of proportion, systemic toxicity, and overlying skin change signal it, and delay costs bowel.
qualifiers.misuse: Repeated attempts at reduction delay surgery and can reduce dead bowel into the abdomen

qualifiers.name: Osmotic diarrhea
qualifiers.definition: Driven by unabsorbed solute, resolves with fasting
qualifiers.established: Observed fasting trial, plus the stool osmotic gap
qualifiers.example: diarrhea stopping with fasting → lactose intolerance
qualifiers.shift: The fasting trial is the discriminator and can be done at the bedside. An elevated stool osmotic gap supports it.

qualifiers.name: Secretory diarrhea
qualifiers.definition: Driven by active secretion, persists with fasting
qualifiers.established: Fasting trial with continued output, plus stool electrolytes
qualifiers.associated: Cholera, neuroendocrine tumors, bile acid diarrhea
qualifiers.example: large-volume diarrhea persisting on fasting → neuroendocrine tumor
qualifiers.shift: Persistence during fasting and large volumes overnight point to a secretagogue and prompt evaluation for hormone-secreting tumors.

qualifiers.name: Inflammatory diarrhea
qualifiers.definition: With blood, mucus, fever, and fecal leukocytes
qualifiers.established: Stool studies including calprotectin, plus endoscopy
qualifiers.example: bloody diarrhea with fever → ulcerative colitis or invasive infection
qualifiers.shift: Directs to mucosal invasion or inflammation, and generally justifies endoscopic evaluation and stool studies rather than symptomatic treatment.

qualifiers.name: Skip lesions
qualifiers.definition: Diseased segments separated by normal mucosa
qualifiers.established: Ileocolonoscopy with segmental biopsies
qualifiers.example: skip lesions → Crohn disease
qualifiers.shift: Discontinuity is a defining feature of Crohn disease and argues against ulcerative colitis, which is continuous from the rectum proximally.

qualifiers.name: Transmural
qualifiers.definition: Inflammation extending through the full bowel wall
qualifiers.established: Cross-sectional imaging or resection histology
qualifiers.example: transmural inflammation with a fistula → Crohn disease
qualifiers.shift: Explains fistulas, abscesses, and strictures, which are Crohn complications and essentially do not occur in the mucosal disease of ulcerative colitis.

qualifiers.name: Stricturing phenotype
qualifiers.definition: Crohn disease dominated by fibrotic narrowing
qualifiers.established: MR enterography distinguishing fibrosis from active inflammation
qualifiers.example: fibrotic stricture → Crohn disease requiring dilation or resection
qualifiers.shift: Fibrotic strictures respond poorly to biologics and often require endoscopic dilation or resection. Phenotype determines whether escalation of medical therapy is even reasonable.
qualifiers.misuse: Biologics escalated for a fibrotic stricture, which will not respond

qualifiers.name: Fistulizing phenotype
qualifiers.established: MR pelvis plus examination under anesthesia
qualifiers.example: perianal fistula → penetrating Crohn disease
qualifiers.shift: Directs toward anti-TNF therapy and surgical assessment, and requires abscess exclusion before immunosuppression.
qualifiers.misuse: Immunosuppression started before an abscess is excluded

qualifiers.name: Backwash ileitis
qualifiers.definition: Mild terminal ileal inflammation in extensive ulcerative colitis
qualifiers.established: Ileocolonoscopy with biopsies of the terminal ileum
qualifiers.example: backwash ileitis → extensive ulcerative colitis
qualifiers.shift: Prevents misclassification as Crohn disease, which would change both medical and surgical planning, notably candidacy for pouch surgery.
qualifiers.misuse: Misclassified as Crohn disease, which changes candidacy for pouch surgery

qualifiers.name: Overt GI bleeding
qualifiers.definition: Visible bleeding as hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia
qualifiers.established: Direct observation of blood
qualifiers.example: hematemesis → peptic ulcer or varices
qualifiers.shift: Directs immediate resuscitation and endoscopy.

qualifiers.name: Obscure GI bleeding
qualifiers.definition: Bleeding persisting after negative upper and lower endoscopy
qualifiers.established: Capsule endoscopy or device-assisted enteroscopy
qualifiers.associated: Small bowel angioectasia, Dieulafoy lesion, small bowel tumor
qualifiers.example: ongoing bleeding after negative endoscopies → small bowel angioectasia
qualifiers.shift: Shifts the search to the small bowel and to capsule endoscopy or enteroscopy rather than repeating the same studies.
qualifiers.misuse: The same upper and lower endoscopies are repeated instead of examining the small bowel

qualifiers.name: Double duct sign
qualifiers.definition: Simultaneous dilation of common bile and pancreatic ducts
qualifiers.established: CT or MRCP showing both ducts dilated
qualifiers.example: double duct sign → pancreatic head adenocarcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Highly concerning for a mass at the ampulla or pancreatic head, even when no mass is directly visible.

qualifiers.name: Fat stranding
qualifiers.definition: Increased attenuation of fat around a structure
qualifiers.established: Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen
qualifiers.example: pericolonic fat stranding → acute diverticulitis
qualifiers.shift: Localizes inflammation anatomically and is often the earliest CT sign, present before an organ looks abnormal.

qualifiers.name: Pneumatosis and portal venous gas
qualifiers.definition: Gas within the bowel wall or portal system
qualifiers.established: CT abdomen with lung windows for bowel wall gas
qualifiers.example: pneumatosis with portal venous gas → bowel infarction
qualifiers.shift: In an unwell patient with abdominal pain this suggests transmural infarction and warrants urgent surgical involvement, though benign pneumatosis exists and context is essential.
qualifiers.misuse: Benign pneumatosis exists; the finding must be read against the clinical picture

qualifiers.name: Nonbloody
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus faecal occult blood testing where relevant
qualifiers.associated: Viral gastroenteritis, osmotic and secretory diarrhea
qualifiers.example: nonbloody watery diarrhea → viral gastroenteritis
qualifiers.shift: Moves away from invasive, inflammatory, and ischemic causes toward secretory and osmotic mechanisms
