qualifiers.misuse: Thyroid hormone given during critical illness

qualifiers.name: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
qualifiers.definition: Low sex hormones with elevated gonadotropins
qualifiers.established: Paired sex hormone and gonadotropin measurement
qualifiers.example: low testosterone with high LH and FSH → primary testicular failure
qualifiers.shift: Localizes the defect to the gonad itself. High FSH and LH with low testosterone or estradiol means primary failure and directs to karyotype and autoimmune evaluation.

qualifiers.name: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
qualifiers.definition: Low sex hormones with low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins
qualifiers.established: Paired measurement plus prolactin and medication review
qualifiers.associated: Pituitary disease, hyperprolactinemia, opioids, functional causes
qualifiers.example: low testosterone with low LH and FSH → pituitary disease or opioid effect
qualifiers.shift: Localizes above the gonad and prompts pituitary imaging, prolactin measurement, and a medication review, notably opioids and glucocorticoids.
qualifiers.misuse: Opioids and glucocorticoids not considered before pituitary imaging

qualifiers.name: Suppressible
qualifiers.definition: Hormone production falls appropriately with a suppression test
qualifiers.established: Formal suppression testing
qualifiers.example: cortisol suppressing on dexamethasone → normal axis
qualifiers.shift: A normal suppression response effectively excludes autonomous secretion and often ends the workup.

qualifiers.name: Autonomous
qualifiers.definition: Hormone production independent of normal feedback
qualifiers.established: Suppressed TSH with focal uptake on scanning
qualifiers.example: autonomous nodule → toxic adenoma
qualifiers.shift: Loss of feedback regulation generally implies a monoclonal lesion and usually requires ablation or resection rather than medical suppression.

qualifiers.name: High radioiodine uptake
qualifiers.definition: Increased tracer uptake by the thyroid
qualifiers.established: Radioiodine uptake and scan
qualifiers.example: diffusely high uptake → Graves disease
qualifiers.shift: Confirms true hyperthyroidism with gland overproduction, so antithyroid drugs and radioiodine are appropriate.

qualifiers.name: Low radioiodine uptake
qualifiers.established: Radioiodine uptake and scan
qualifiers.example: low uptake with thyrotoxicosis → thyroiditis or exogenous hormone
qualifiers.shift: Indicates release of preformed hormone or an exogenous source. Antithyroid drugs are useless here, which is why the scan changes management rather than merely confirming it.

qualifiers.name: Ketosis-prone
qualifiers.established: History of ketoacidosis plus antibody and C-peptide testing
qualifiers.example: diabetic ketoacidosis at presentation → ketosis-prone diabetes
qualifiers.shift: Predicts insulin dependence and vulnerability during illness, independent of the nominal diabetes classification.

qualifiers.name: Acquired
qualifiers.definition: Developed after birth rather than inherited
qualifiers.established: History plus absence of family history and genetic markers
qualifiers.example: acquired factor inhibitor → autoimmune or malignancy-associated
qualifiers.shift: Redirects from genetic testing toward an underlying trigger such as autoimmunity, malignancy, or drugs

qualifiers.name: Familial
qualifiers.definition: Occurring more often within a family
qualifiers.established: Three-generation family history
qualifiers.example: familial hypercholesterolemia → cascade screening of relatives
qualifiers.shift: Extends implications beyond the patient. Family history is cheap, underperformed, and frequently changes management
qualifiers.misuse: Family history taken as a yes-or-no question rather than constructed as a pedigree

qualifiers.name: Responsive
qualifiers.established: Documented objective improvement on therapy
qualifiers.example: levodopa-responsive parkinsonism → idiopathic Parkinson disease
qualifiers.shift: Therapeutic response can be diagnostic. Poor levodopa response argues against idiopathic Parkinson disease and toward an atypical syndrome
qualifiers.misuse: Response claimed without an objective before-and-after measure

qualifiers.name: Treatment-resistant
qualifiers.established: Documented failure of adequately dosed and adhered-to therapy
qualifiers.example: blood pressure above target on three agents including a diuretic → resistant hypertension
qualifiers.shift: A formal definition with a specific workup attached. In hypertension it triggers evaluation for secondary causes
qualifiers.misuse: Declared before adherence, dosing, and white-coat effect have been excluded

qualifiers.name: Overt
qualifiers.established: Both the trophic hormone and the target hormone abnormal
qualifiers.example: raised TSH with low free T4 → overt hypothyroidism
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes disease requiring treatment from subclinical abnormality, where treatment thresholds are contested

qualifiers.name: Systemic
qualifiers.established: Findings in two or more organ systems
qualifiers.example: rash with nephritis and neuropathy → systemic vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: Multisystem involvement is the single most useful trigger to stop thinking about local causes and start thinking about a unifying systemic diagnosis

qualifiers.name: Catabolic
qualifiers.established: Weight and muscle loss despite intake, plus a negative nitrogen balance
qualifiers.associated: Malignancy, critical illness, thyrotoxicosis, advanced organ failure
qualifiers.example: weight loss despite preserved appetite → catabolic state
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes loss from inadequate intake, which responds to feeding, from true catabolism, which does not
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as a nutrition problem alone; in cachexia feeding does not reverse the process

qualifiers.name: Hypermetabolic
qualifiers.established: Weight loss with increased appetite, tachycardia, heat intolerance
qualifiers.example: weight loss with increased appetite → thyrotoxicosis
qualifiers.shift: Weight loss with a preserved or increased appetite is a short differential, headed by hyperthyroidism and malabsorption

qualifiers.name: Hypometabolic
qualifiers.established: Weight gain, cold intolerance, bradycardia, slowed reflexes
qualifiers.example: cold intolerance with bradycardia and slow relaxing reflexes → hypothyroidism
qualifiers.shift: The mirror of hypermetabolic, and the delayed relaxation phase of the ankle reflex is a classic and specific bedside sign

qualifiers.name: Toxic-appearing
qualifiers.definition: Ill, lethargic, poorly perfused, or agitated on first impression
qualifiers.established: End-of-bed assessment before touching the patient
qualifiers.example: toxic appearance → sepsis
qualifiers.shift: A gestalt judgment that reliably outperforms individual vital signs at the front door. Should accelerate evaluation and empiric therapy before the workup returns.

qualifiers.name: Well-appearing
qualifiers.established: End-of-bed assessment, weighed against vital signs
qualifiers.example: well appearance → self-limited illness
qualifiers.shift: Genuinely reassuring in most contexts, but a documented trap in early sepsis, compensated shock in the young, and mesenteric ischemia. Never allow it to override an abnormal physiologic parameter.
qualifiers.misuse: Used to override abnormal physiology; a documented trap in early sepsis and mesenteric ischemia

qualifiers.name: Cachectic
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus documented weight trajectory
qualifiers.associated: Malignancy, advanced heart or lung disease, HIV
qualifiers.example: cachexia → malignancy or advanced organ failure
qualifiers.shift: Implies a catabolic process over months and raises malignancy, chronic infection, and advanced organ failure. Independently predicts poor outcomes.

qualifiers.name: Diaphoretic
qualifiers.established: Inspection and touch
qualifiers.associated: ACS, hypoglycemia, sepsis, thyroid storm, withdrawal
qualifiers.example: diaphoresis with chest pain → acute myocardial infarction
qualifiers.shift: A sympathetic surge. In chest pain it meaningfully raises the likelihood of infarction.

qualifiers.name: Icteric
qualifiers.definition: Yellow discoloration of sclerae and skin
qualifiers.established: Inspect the sclerae in natural light
qualifiers.example: scleral icterus → hyperbilirubinemia
qualifiers.shift: Detectable in the sclerae at lower bilirubin levels than in skin, so scleral examination is the more sensitive test.
qualifiers.misuse: Skin inspected instead; sclerae are more sensitive and less affected by skin tone

qualifiers.name: Central cyanosis
qualifiers.definition: Bluish discoloration of lips, tongue, and mucous membranes
qualifiers.established: Inspect the tongue and oral mucosa
qualifiers.example: central cyanosis → arterial hypoxemia or methemoglobinemia
qualifiers.shift: Reflects arterial desaturation and is a systemic problem. Requires roughly 5 g/dL of deoxygenated hemoglobin, so it appears late in anemia and early in polycythemia.
qualifiers.misuse: Requires about 5 g/dL of deoxygenated hemoglobin, so it appears late in anemia

qualifiers.name: Peripheral cyanosis
qualifiers.established: Compare peripheries with the tongue
qualifiers.associated: Low output, cold exposure, peripheral vascular disease
qualifiers.example: peripheral cyanosis with warm core → low cardiac output
qualifiers.shift: Reflects increased peripheral extraction with normal arterial saturation. A perfusion problem, not an oxygenation problem.

qualifiers.name: Clubbing
qualifiers.definition: Loss of the nail-fold angle with increased nail bed fluctuance
qualifiers.established: Schamroth window and nail bed fluctuance
qualifiers.associated: Bronchiectasis, lung cancer, ILD, cyanotic heart disease, cirrhosis, IBD
qualifiers.example: clubbing in a smoker with dyspnea → lung cancer or bronchiectasis
qualifiers.shift: Notably absent in uncomplicated COPD and asthma, so its presence in a smoker with dyspnea should redirect toward malignancy, bronchiectasis, or fibrosis.
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to COPD, which does not cause clubbing

qualifiers.name: Pitting edema
qualifiers.established: Sustained pressure for at least ten seconds over a bony prominence
qualifiers.associated: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, venous disease
qualifiers.example: bilateral pitting edema → heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Indicates increased interstitial water with low protein content. Combined with laterality it is highly directive: bilateral pitting suggests systemic causes, unilateral suggests venous obstruction.
qualifiers.misuse: Pressed too briefly, so pitting is missed

qualifiers.name: Nonpitting edema
qualifiers.established: Sustained pressure producing no indentation
qualifiers.example: nonpitting limb swelling → lymphedema
qualifiers.shift: Redirects away from the common cardiac and renal causes toward lymphatic obstruction and thyroid disease, an entirely different workup.
qualifiers.misuse: Diuretics given for lymphedema, which does not respond

qualifiers.name: Anasarca
qualifiers.definition: Generalized massive edema including trunk and face
qualifiers.established: Examination of dependent areas, trunk, and face
qualifiers.associated: Nephrotic syndrome, severe heart failure, hepatic failure
qualifiers.example: anasarca → nephrotic syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Implies severe hypoalbuminemia or profound volume overload and marks advanced disease.

qualifiers.name: Fluctuant
qualifiers.established: Bimanual palpation for a transmitted fluid wave, or ultrasound
qualifiers.example: fluctuant swelling → abscess
qualifiers.shift: Indicates a drainable collection. Antibiotics alone are usually insufficient; this is a procedural finding.

qualifiers.name: Indurated
qualifiers.definition: Firm, thickened tissue without discrete fluid
qualifiers.established: Palpation for firmness without a fluid wave
qualifiers.example: induration without fluctuance → cellulitis
qualifiers.shift: Suggests inflammatory infiltration or fibrosis rather than a drainable collection.

qualifiers.name: Fixed
qualifiers.definition: Not mobile relative to surrounding tissue
qualifiers.established: Attempt to move the node against underlying tissue
qualifiers.example: fixed hard node → metastatic carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Suggests invasion beyond the capsule. A hard, fixed, nontender node is a malignancy concern until proven otherwise.

qualifiers.name: Mobile
qualifiers.established: Palpation assessing mobility and consistency
qualifiers.example: mobile rubbery node → reactive lymphadenopathy
qualifiers.shift: Suggests a lesion that has not invaded its surroundings, and generally favors a benign process.

qualifiers.name: Matted
qualifiers.definition: Multiple nodes adherent to one another
qualifiers.established: Palpation for adherence between adjacent nodes
qualifiers.example: matted cervical nodes → tuberculous lymphadenitis
qualifiers.shift: Implies periadenitis and capsular breach. Uncommon in reactive lymphadenopathy and should prompt biopsy.

qualifiers.name: Bruit
qualifiers.established: Auscultate with the bell during held breath
qualifiers.associated: Carotid stenosis, renal artery stenosis, AV fistula
qualifiers.example: carotid bruit → carotid stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Indicates turbulent flow but correlates imperfectly with stenosis severity; a very tight stenosis may be silent.
qualifiers.misuse: Correlates poorly with severity; a critical stenosis may be silent

qualifiers.name: Thrill
qualifiers.definition: Palpable vibration over a vessel or the precordium
qualifiers.established: Palpate the precordium with the palm
qualifiers.associated: Severe valvular lesions, VSD, AV fistula
qualifiers.example: systolic thrill → severe valvular lesion or VSD
qualifiers.shift: A palpable thrill corresponds to at least a grade 4 murmur and reliably indicates a hemodynamically significant lesion.

qualifiers.name: Euvolemic
qualifiers.established: JVP, skin turgor, mucous membranes, orthostatic vitals, weight trend
qualifiers.example: euvolemic hyponatremia → SIADH
qualifiers.shift: Volume status is the first branch point in hyponatremia and determines the entire subsequent workup and treatment
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed by one sign alone; clinical volume assessment is unreliable unless several findings are combined

qualifiers.name: Hypovolemic
qualifiers.established: Flat JVP, orthostatic change, dry membranes, low urine sodium
qualifiers.example: hypovolemic hyponatremia → gastrointestinal losses
qualifiers.shift: Directs toward saline rather than fluid restriction, the opposite of the treatment for SIADH
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with SIADH, and treating one as the other makes the sodium worse

qualifiers.name: Hypervolemic
qualifiers.established: Elevated JVP, edema, ascites, weight gain, crackles
qualifiers.example: hypervolemic hyponatremia → decompensated heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Indicates the effective arterial volume is low despite total body overload, which is why these patients are both wet and sodium-avid
qualifiers.misuse: Total body water and effective circulating volume conflated, which makes the physiology look contradictory

qualifiers.name: Serous
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of drainage
qualifiers.example: serous wound drainage → seroma
qualifiers.shift: Argues against infection, which typically produces purulent or turbid fluid

qualifiers.name: Serosanguineous
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of drainage
qualifiers.example: serosanguineous drainage → expected postoperative finding
qualifiers.shift: Usually expected early after surgery. A change from serosanguineous to purulent is the finding that matters

diagnoses.name: Acute coronary syndrome
diagnoses.why: Exertional pressure with radiation and diaphoresis is a supply-demand story with autonomic activation; no single element is specific but the set is
diagnoses.mimic: Pericarditis → positional and pleuritic rather than exertional

diagnoses.name: Aortic dissection
diagnoses.why: Maximal-at-onset severity plus migration and pulse asymmetry is mechanical, not ischemic
diagnoses.mimic: STEMI → crescendo rather than maximal at onset, and symmetric pulses

diagnoses.name: Severe aortic stenosis
diagnoses.why: A slowly progressive fixed obstruction produces exertional symptoms and a delayed weak upstroke
diagnoses.mimic: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy → louder with Valsalva, and a brisk bifid upstroke

diagnoses.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
diagnoses.why: Dynamic obstruction worsens with reduced preload, the reverse of fixed obstruction
diagnoses.mimic: Aortic stenosis → softer with Valsalva, radiates to carotids

diagnoses.name: HFrEF decompensation
diagnoses.why: Volume redistribution when supine plus a compliant dilated ventricle and raised filling pressures
diagnoses.mimic: COPD exacerbation → no orthopnea, normal JVP, hyperresonant rather than dull

diagnoses.name: HFpEF
diagnoses.why: Congestion with a stiff ventricle: atrial contraction against noncompliance gives S4, not S3
diagnoses.mimic: HFrEF → S3 and reduced ejection fraction

diagnoses.name: Cardiac tamponade
diagnoses.why: Ventricular interdependence under external constraint, with the heart swinging in fluid
diagnoses.mimic: Constrictive pericarditis → Kussmaul sign present, pulsus paradoxus usually absent

diagnoses.name: Constrictive pericarditis
diagnoses.why: A rigid pericardium prevents inspiratory accommodation, hence the paradoxical JVP rise
diagnoses.mimic: Restrictive cardiomyopathy → markedly elevated BNP, no septal bounce

diagnoses.name: Acute pericarditis
cluster: diffuse ST elevation with PR depression
diagnoses.why: Inflamed parietal pericardium with somatic innervation, hence sharp and position-dependent
diagnoses.mimic: STEMI → territorial ST elevation with reciprocal change, not diffuse

diagnoses.name: Infective endocarditis
diagnoses.why: Continuous bacteremia from an endovascular focus seeding distant sites
diagnoses.mimic: Culture-negative endocarditis → same cluster with negative cultures, prompting serology

diagnoses.name: Atrial fibrillation
diagnoses.why: Disorganized atrial activity, so no organized atrial contraction and no repeating pattern
diagnoses.mimic: Multifocal atrial tachycardia → also irregular but with three distinct P morphologies

diagnoses.name: Ventricular tachycardia
diagnoses.why: Ventricular origin with independent atrial activity, visible in the neck and on the strip
diagnoses.mimic: SVT with aberrancy → no AV dissociation, often prior identical bundle branch morphology

diagnoses.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
diagnoses.why: The mismatch between electrical smallness and anatomic thickness is the signature
diagnoses.mimic: Hypertensive heart disease → voltage proportionate to wall thickness

diagnoses.name: Critical limb ischemia
diagnoses.why: Perfusion fails at baseline demand, hence pain without activity and relief with dependency
diagnoses.mimic: Claudication → exertional only, resolves with rest within minutes

diagnoses.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White with atrial fibrillation
cluster: with a delta wave in sinus rhythm
diagnoses.why: Conduction down an accessory pathway bypassing the AV node, so rate is limited only by pathway refractoriness
diagnoses.mimic: Atrial fibrillation with bundle branch block → monomorphic wide complexes at a rate the AV node can explain

diagnoses.name: Complete heart block
cluster: with AV dissociation and cannon a waves
diagnoses.why: Atria and ventricles beating independently, visible in the neck and on the rhythm strip
diagnoses.mimic: Sinus bradycardia → P waves conduct, no cannon a waves

diagnoses.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
cluster: after an emotional or physical stressor
and apical ballooning but unobstructed coronaries
diagnoses.why: Catecholamine-mediated stunning in a non-coronary distribution, so the wall motion crosses territories
diagnoses.mimic: STEMI → wall motion abnormality confined to one coronary territory, culprit lesion present

diagnoses.name: Acute myocarditis
diagnoses.why: Diffuse myocardial inflammation, so dysfunction is global rather than territorial
diagnoses.mimic: Acute coronary syndrome → territorial wall motion abnormality, exertional history

diagnoses.name: Aortic regurgitation, acute
diagnoses.why: Sudden regurgitation into an uncompliant ventricle, so the classic chronic signs are absent
diagnoses.mimic: Chronic aortic regurgitation → wide pulse pressure, collapsing pulse, long murmur

diagnoses.name: Mitral stenosis, rheumatic
cluster: progressive exertional dyspnea with a low-pitched apical diastolic rumble and an opening snap
diagnoses.why: Fixed inflow obstruction with pliable leaflets, so the snap precedes the rumble
diagnoses.mimic: Left atrial myxoma → positional symptoms, tumor plop rather than opening snap

diagnoses.name: Prosthetic valve thrombosis
diagnoses.why: Thrombus restricting leaflet motion, so the mechanical click softens or disappears
diagnoses.mimic: Prosthetic valve endocarditis → febrile, bacteremic, vegetation on imaging

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
cluster: progressive exertional dyspnea with a loud P2
diagnoses.why: Pre-capillary obstruction, so the right heart fails while the left remains normal
diagnoses.mimic: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction → elevated filling pressures, responds to diuresis

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary embolism
diagnoses.why: Sudden vascular occlusion producing dead space and pleural irritation without consolidation
diagnoses.mimic: Pneumonia → productive, febrile, consolidative rather than clear on imaging

diagnoses.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
diagnoses.why: Alveolar filling with an inflammatory response, conducting sound abnormally
diagnoses.mimic: Heart failure → bilateral, dependent, Kerley B lines, orthopnea

diagnoses.name: COPD exacerbation
diagnoses.why: Diffuse small-airway obstruction with pump failure rather than oxygenation failure
diagnoses.mimic: Asthma → reversible obstruction, younger, no chronic hypercapnia

diagnoses.name: Asthma
diagnoses.why: Variable and reversible obstruction with diurnal and trigger-related variation
diagnoses.mimic: Vocal cord dysfunction → inspiratory stridor, no reversibility, flow-volume loop truncated

diagnoses.name: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
diagnoses.why: Established peripheral basal fibrosis with irreversible architectural distortion
diagnoses.mimic: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis → upper-lobe predominant with mosaic attenuation and air trapping

diagnoses.name: Sarcoidosis
diagnoses.why: Non-caseating granulomas tracking along lymphatics
diagnoses.mimic: Tuberculosis → cavitary, apical, tree-in-bud, positive microbiology

diagnoses.name: Tension pneumothorax
cluster: unilateral hyperresonance with absent breath sounds
diagnoses.why: Progressive one-way air accumulation compressing mediastinal structures
diagnoses.mimic: Massive effusion → dull rather than hyperresonant to percussion

diagnoses.name: Empyema
diagnoses.why: Infected pleural fluid organizing into compartments
diagnoses.mimic: Simple parapneumonic effusion → free-flowing and non-loculated on ultrasound

diagnoses.name: ARDS
diagnoses.why: Diffuse alveolar damage causing shunt that does not correct with oxygen
diagnoses.mimic: Cardiogenic edema → elevated JVP, S3, responds to diuresis

diagnoses.name: Bronchiectasis
diagnoses.why: Permanently dilated airways with chronic infection and impaired clearance
diagnoses.mimic: COPD → less sputum volume, no clubbing, no tram-track dilatation

diagnoses.name: Pneumocystis pneumonia
diagnoses.why: Alveolar filling in a T-cell-deficient host, with gas exchange failing before imaging looks dramatic
diagnoses.mimic: Bacterial pneumonia → acute, productive, focal and consolidative

diagnoses.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
diagnoses.why: Repetitive upper airway collapse during sleep with daytime consequences
diagnoses.mimic: Central sleep apnea → absent respiratory effort rather than obstructed effort

diagnoses.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
cluster: upper-lobe predominant ground-glass with mosaic attenuation and air trapping
diagnoses.why: Small airway centred inflammation from inhaled antigen, hence air trapping and upper zone predominance
diagnoses.mimic: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis → basal, subpleural, honeycombing, no exposure history

diagnoses.name: Organizing pneumonia
diagnoses.why: Alveolar organizing exudate in a peripheral distribution, steroid responsive rather than antibiotic responsive
diagnoses.mimic: Bacterial pneumonia → responds to antibiotics, lobar rather than peripheral banding

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
cluster: progressive dyspnea with crazy paving on CT and disproportionately mild examination
diagnoses.why: Alveolar filling with surfactant material, producing a characteristic imaging pattern
diagnoses.mimic: Pneumocystis pneumonia → immunocompromised host, exertional desaturation, ground-glass without septal thickening

diagnoses.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
cluster: with lower-zone emphysema in a young patient and possible liver disease
diagnoses.why: Lower zone rather than upper zone emphysema, and onset decades early
diagnoses.mimic: COPD from smoking → upper zone predominant, older, no hepatic involvement

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary edema, cardiogenic
cluster: central-predominant opacities with Kerley B lines
diagnoses.why: Hydrostatic transudation with raised left atrial pressure, so cardiac signs accompany the imaging
diagnoses.mimic: ARDS → bilateral but peripheral, no elevated JVP, hypoxemia resistant to oxygen

diagnoses.name: Massive pulmonary embolism
cluster: with right ventricular strain and a normal chest radiograph
diagnoses.why: Sudden obstruction of pulmonary flow, so hypoxemia and shock occur with a clear film
diagnoses.mimic: Tension pneumothorax → unilateral hyperresonance with absent breath sounds

diagnoses.name: Aspiration pneumonitis
cluster: gravity-determined opacities after a witnessed aspiration
diagnoses.why: Chemical injury in gravity-dependent segments, preceding any infection
diagnoses.mimic: Aspiration pneumonia → febrile, later, with polymicrobial infection

diagnoses.name: Lung cancer, non-small cell
diagnoses.why: Slow local growth with spiculation from desmoplastic reaction, plus constitutional features
diagnoses.mimic: Pulmonary tuberculoma → calcified, apical, stable over time

diagnoses.name: Appendicitis
cluster: migratory from periumbilical to right lower quadrant
diagnoses.why: Visceral inflammation reaching the parietal peritoneum, which is why the pain moves and localizes
diagnoses.mimic: Mesenteric adenitis → no migration, no localized peritonism

diagnoses.name: Acute cholecystitis
diagnoses.why: Cystic duct obstruction progressing to wall inflammation, so colic becomes constant
diagnoses.mimic: Biliary colic → remains colicky and self-limited, no fever or Murphy sign

diagnoses.name: Ascending cholangitis
diagnoses.why: Obstructed and infected biliary tree with hematogenous spread
diagnoses.mimic: Cholecystitis → no jaundice, no cholestatic laboratory pattern

diagnoses.name: Acute pancreatitis
diagnoses.why: Retroperitoneal inflammation, hence constant boring pain with posture dependence
diagnoses.mimic: Perforated ulcer → abrupt, free air, board-like rigidity

diagnoses.name: Small bowel obstruction
diagnoses.why: Peristalsis working against a mechanical block, with progressive proximal stasis
diagnoses.mimic: Ileus → absent bowel sounds, no transition point on imaging

diagnoses.name: Acute mesenteric ischemia
diagnoses.why: Ischemic visceral pain precedes peritoneal signs because the peritoneum is spared until infarction
diagnoses.mimic: Gastroenteritis → tenderness proportionate to reported pain

diagnoses.name: Peptic ulcer disease
diagnoses.why: Acid-related mucosal injury, symptomatic when the stomach is empty
diagnoses.mimic: Gastric malignancy → progressive, constant, with weight loss and early satiety

diagnoses.name: Achalasia
cluster: dysphagia to solids and liquids from the outset
diagnoses.why: A motility disorder, so both phases fail equally from the beginning
diagnoses.mimic: Esophageal carcinoma → solids first, then liquids, with rapid weight loss

diagnoses.name: Esophageal carcinoma
diagnoses.why: Mechanical narrowing progressing through the lumen over months
diagnoses.mimic: Peptic stricture → solid dysphagia but non-progressive with a long reflux history

diagnoses.name: Ulcerative colitis
diagnoses.why: Continuous mucosal inflammation extending proximally from the rectum
diagnoses.mimic: Crohn colitis → skip lesions, transmural, rectal sparing, perianal disease

diagnoses.name: Crohn disease
diagnoses.why: Discontinuous full-thickness inflammation, hence penetrating and fibrotic complications
diagnoses.mimic: Ulcerative colitis → continuous and mucosal, no fistulas

diagnoses.name: Clostridioides difficile colitis
diagnoses.why: Toxin-mediated colitis following antimicrobial disruption of flora
diagnoses.mimic: Ischemic colitis → segmental, watershed distribution, older vasculopath

diagnoses.name: Decompensated cirrhosis
diagnoses.why: Portal hypertension plus failed synthetic and detoxifying function
diagnoses.mimic: Constrictive pericarditis → also high SAAG ascites but with elevated JVP and Kussmaul sign

diagnoses.name: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
diagnoses.why: Translocation into pre-existing ascites, often without peritoneal signs
diagnoses.mimic: Secondary peritonitis → polymicrobial, higher protein, requires imaging and surgery

diagnoses.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
diagnoses.why: Immune-mediated small duct destruction producing itch before jaundice
diagnoses.mimic: Primary sclerosing cholangitis → beaded ducts on MRCP, associated with IBD, AMA negative

diagnoses.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
diagnoses.why: Interface hepatitis from adaptive immunity against hepatocytes
diagnoses.mimic: Drug-induced liver injury → temporal drug relationship, improves on dechallenge

diagnoses.name: Variceal hemorrhage
cluster: hematemesis with hemodynamic instability in a patient with known portal hypertension
diagnoses.why: Rupture of a high-pressure portosystemic collateral, so bleeding is brisk and painless
diagnoses.mimic: Peptic ulcer bleeding → epigastric pain history, no stigmata of chronic liver disease

diagnoses.name: Acute liver failure
cluster: and encephalopathy in the absence of prior liver disease
diagnoses.why: Massive hepatocyte loss, defined by coagulopathy plus encephalopathy within weeks of jaundice
diagnoses.mimic: Decompensated cirrhosis → chronic stigmata, longer course, portal hypertension

diagnoses.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
cluster: with asterixis and reversal of sleep pattern in a patient with cirrhosis
diagnoses.why: Metabolic encephalopathy with negative myoclonus rather than focal signs
diagnoses.mimic: Structural intracranial lesion → focal deficits, does not fluctuate with lactulose

diagnoses.name: Sigmoid volvulus
cluster: tympanitic abdomen with a coffee-bean loop on imaging in an elderly constipated patient
diagnoses.why: Torsion of a redundant sigmoid on its mesentery, producing closed-loop obstruction
diagnoses.mimic: Pseudo-obstruction → dilated colon without a transition point or whirl sign

diagnoses.name: Perforated peptic ulcer
cluster: with board-like rigidity and free air
diagnoses.why: Sudden peritoneal contamination, so pain is maximal at onset and the abdomen becomes rigid
diagnoses.mimic: Acute pancreatitis → constant boring pain radiating to the back, no free air

diagnoses.name: Ischemic colitis
cluster: crampy left-sided pain with bloody diarrhea in a watershed distribution in an older vasculopath
diagnoses.why: Hypoperfusion of watershed segments, so it is segmental rather than diffuse
diagnoses.mimic: Infectious colitis → diffuse, febrile, positive stool studies

diagnoses.name: Celiac disease
cluster: and positive tissue transglutaminase on a gluten-containing diet
diagnoses.why: Mucosal malabsorption, so deficiencies appear alongside the bowel symptoms
diagnoses.mimic: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency → steatorrhea without iron deficiency or serology

diagnoses.name: Prerenal azotemia
diagnoses.why: Intact tubules avidly reabsorbing sodium in response to hypoperfusion
diagnoses.mimic: Acute tubular necrosis → muddy brown casts and FENa above 2%

diagnoses.name: Acute tubular necrosis
diagnoses.why: Tubular epithelial injury shedding casts, with lost concentrating ability
diagnoses.mimic: Prerenal → bland sediment and a response to volume

diagnoses.name: Acute interstitial nephritis
diagnoses.why: Drug-triggered interstitial inflammation without glomerular involvement
diagnoses.mimic: Pyelonephritis → febrile, flank pain, positive urine culture

diagnoses.name: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
diagnoses.why: Severe glomerular injury with extracapillary proliferation over days to weeks
diagnoses.mimic: Chronic glomerulonephritis → slow decline, small kidneys, bland sediment

diagnoses.name: Nephrotic syndrome
diagnoses.why: Podocyte injury permitting massive protein loss without inflammation
diagnoses.mimic: Nephritic syndrome → hematuria with RBC casts and hypertension, lesser proteinuria

diagnoses.name: Lupus nephritis
diagnoses.why: Immune complex deposition consuming complement across multiple immunoglobulin classes
diagnoses.mimic: ANCA vasculitis → pauci-immune with normal complement

diagnoses.name: Anti-GBM disease
diagnoses.why: Antibody bound continuously along the basement membrane in kidney and lung
diagnoses.mimic: ANCA vasculitis → pauci-immune, granular or absent staining

diagnoses.name: Obstructive uropathy
diagnoses.why: Mechanical blockage of outflow with preserved parenchyma early
diagnoses.mimic: Prerenal → responds to volume, no hydronephrosis

diagnoses.name: Distal renal tubular acidosis
diagnoses.why: Failure of distal acidification with impaired ammonium excretion
diagnoses.mimic: Diarrheal bicarbonate loss → negative urine anion gap, appropriately acidic urine

diagnoses.name: Hepatorenal syndrome
cluster: with bland sediment in decompensated cirrhosis and no response to volume
diagnoses.why: Functional renal failure from splanchnic vasodilation, so the kidney is structurally normal
diagnoses.mimic: Prerenal azotemia → responds to albumin and volume expansion

diagnoses.name: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury
cluster: with bland sediment and spontaneous recovery
diagnoses.why: Temporal association with contrast and a self-limited course
diagnoses.mimic: Atheroembolic disease → eosinophilia, livedo, progressive rather than recovering

diagnoses.name: Cholesterol atheroembolism
cluster: stepwise renal decline after an arterial procedure
diagnoses.why: Showers of cholesterol crystals, so skin, kidney, and eosinophils are affected together
diagnoses.mimic: Contrast nephropathy → immediate, recovers, no skin findings

diagnoses.name: IgA nephropathy
cluster: with synpharyngitic gross hematuria within days of an upper respiratory infection
diagnoses.why: Mucosal IgA response, so hematuria coincides with rather than follows infection
diagnoses.mimic: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis → latent period of 1 to 3 weeks, low complement

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
cluster: nephrotic-range proteinuria in an adult with anti-PLA2R antibodies
diagnoses.why: Subepithelial immune deposits producing heavy proteinuria without inflammation
diagnoses.mimic: Minimal change disease → abrupt onset, steroid responsive, normal light microscopy

diagnoses.name: Rhabdomyolysis
cluster: and heme-positive urine without red cells
diagnoses.why: Myoglobin producing a dipstick-positive, microscopy-negative urine
diagnoses.mimic: Hemolysis → heme-positive urine with pink plasma rather than pigmented casts

diagnoses.name: Hyperkalemia, severe
cluster: with peaked T waves progressing to a widened QRS and a sine wave
diagnoses.why: Membrane depolarization producing a stereotyped ECG progression
diagnoses.mimic: Hypocalcemia → prolonged QT without peaked T waves

diagnoses.name: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
diagnoses.why: Bilateral cystic replacement over decades, with extrarenal associations
diagnoses.mimic: Simple renal cysts → few, non-enlarging, normal renal function

diagnoses.name: Ischemic stroke
diagnoses.why: Sudden loss of function in one vascular territory, with cytotoxic edema within minutes
diagnoses.mimic: Migraine aura → positive symptoms marching over minutes, fully reversible

diagnoses.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
diagnoses.why: Instantaneous arterial rupture into the subarachnoid space with meningeal irritation
diagnoses.mimic: Migraine → builds over minutes to hours, recurrent and stereotyped

diagnoses.name: Transient ischemic attack
diagnoses.why: Reversible ischemia without infarction, so function returns entirely
diagnoses.mimic: Focal seizure → positive symptoms with postictal deficit rather than immediate recovery

diagnoses.name: Guillain-Barré syndrome
diagnoses.why: Immune attack on roots and peripheral nerves after an antecedent infection
diagnoses.mimic: Transverse myelitis → sensory level with hyperreflexia below it

diagnoses.name: Multiple sclerosis
diagnoses.why: Recurrent CNS demyelination at separate sites and separate times
diagnoses.mimic: ADEM → monophasic, often post-infectious, no new lesions over time

diagnoses.name: Myasthenia gravis
diagnoses.why: Neuromuscular junction failure that worsens with use and recovers with rest
diagnoses.mimic: Lambert-Eaton → transient facilitation with brief exercise, autonomic features

diagnoses.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
cluster: mixed upper and lower motor neuron
diagnoses.why: Simultaneous corticospinal and anterior horn degeneration with sensory sparing
diagnoses.mimic: Cervical myelopathy → sensory level present, no tongue fasciculations

diagnoses.name: Cervical myelopathy
diagnoses.why: Cord compression producing upper motor neuron signs below the lesion
diagnoses.mimic: Peripheral neuropathy → hyporeflexic and length-dependent, no sensory level

diagnoses.name: Cauda equina syndrome
diagnoses.why: Compression of multiple lumbosacral roots below the cord
diagnoses.mimic: Conus medullaris lesion → mixed upper and lower motor neuron findings, earlier sphincter loss

diagnoses.name: Bacterial meningitis
diagnoses.why: Purulent inflammation of the meninges with bacterial glucose consumption
diagnoses.mimic: Viral meningitis → lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal glucose

diagnoses.name: Herpes simplex encephalitis
diagnoses.why: Necrotizing temporal lobe infection producing behavioral change and seizures
diagnoses.mimic: Autoimmune encephalitis → subacute, psychiatric prodrome, antibody-positive

diagnoses.name: Parkinson disease
diagnoses.why: Asymmetric nigrostriatal loss with a movement that damps on action
diagnoses.mimic: Essential tremor → symmetric postural tremor, no bradykinesia

diagnoses.name: Delirium
diagnoses.why: Global cerebral dysfunction from a systemic insult, hence variability over hours
diagnoses.mimic: Dementia → chronic, insidious, stable attention

diagnoses.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus
diagnoses.why: Ventricular enlargement disproportionate to atrophy, gait affected first
diagnoses.mimic: Parkinson disease → rest tremor, asymmetric, responds to levodopa

diagnoses.name: Giant cell arteritis
diagnoses.why: Large-vessel granulomatous inflammation of cranial branches
diagnoses.mimic: Tension headache → chronic, no systemic features, normal inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
cluster: positional headache with papilledema and an opening pressure over 25 in a young obese woman
diagnoses.why: Raised pressure without a mass, so imaging is normal and the pressure is the finding
diagnoses.mimic: Venous sinus thrombosis → filling defect on venography, same clinical picture

diagnoses.name: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
cluster: progressive headache with seizures and focal deficits crossing arterial territories
diagnoses.why: Venous rather than arterial occlusion, so the deficit does not respect an arterial territory
diagnoses.mimic: Arterial stroke → deficit confined to one arterial territory

diagnoses.name: Wernicke encephalopathy, neurologic presentation
cluster: and ataxia in a malnourished patient
diagnoses.why: A specific triad from thiamine deficiency injuring periaqueductal grey
diagnoses.mimic: Alcohol intoxication → no ophthalmoplegia, resolves with time

diagnoses.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
diagnoses.why: Brief lancinating pain in a trigeminal division with cutaneous triggers
diagnoses.mimic: Atypical facial pain → constant, aching, not trigger-dependent

diagnoses.name: Bell palsy
cluster: unilateral facial weakness including the forehead
diagnoses.why: Lower motor neuron seventh nerve palsy, so the forehead is involved
diagnoses.mimic: Cortical stroke → forehead spared, other deficits present

diagnoses.name: Status epilepticus
cluster: continuous or recurrent seizures beyond five minutes without recovery between
diagnoses.why: Failure of seizure termination mechanisms, defined by duration
diagnoses.mimic: Psychogenic non-epileptic seizure → preserved awareness, asynchronous movements, no postictal acidosis

diagnoses.name: Lewy body dementia
diagnoses.why: Fluctuation and early hallucinations distinguish it from Alzheimer disease
diagnoses.mimic: Alzheimer disease → steady decline, hallucinations late, no early parkinsonism

diagnoses.name: Subdural hematoma, chronic
cluster: fluctuating confusion in an older or anticoagulated patient after minor trauma
diagnoses.why: Slow venous bleeding, so the interval between trauma and symptoms is long
diagnoses.mimic: Normal pressure hydrocephalus → gait first, ventriculomegaly without a collection

diagnoses.name: Iron deficiency anemia
diagnoses.why: Depleted stores limiting hemoglobin synthesis, so cells are small and pale
diagnoses.mimic: Thalassemia trait → microcytic with normal or high red cell count and normal iron studies

diagnoses.name: Anemia of chronic disease
diagnoses.why: Hepcidin-driven iron sequestration with adequate but unavailable stores
diagnoses.mimic: Iron deficiency → low ferritin, responds to oral iron

diagnoses.name: B12 deficiency
diagnoses.why: Impaired DNA synthesis plus subacute combined degeneration
diagnoses.mimic: Folate deficiency → same hematology without neurologic findings

diagnoses.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
diagnoses.why: ADAMTS13 deficiency causing platelet-rich microthrombi and mechanical hemolysis
diagnoses.mimic: DIC → prolonged PT and aPTT with low fibrinogen; TTP has normal coagulation

diagnoses.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
diagnoses.why: Simultaneous systemic activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis
diagnoses.mimic: TTP → normal fibrinogen and coagulation times

diagnoses.name: Immune thrombocytopenia
diagnoses.why: Peripheral immune destruction of platelets alone
diagnoses.mimic: Marrow failure → multilineage cytopenias

diagnoses.name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
cluster: thrombocytopenic with a fall of over 50%
diagnoses.why: Antibody-mediated platelet activation, so patients clot rather than bleed
diagnoses.mimic: Other drug-induced thrombocytopenia → bleeding phenotype, no thrombosis

diagnoses.name: Multiple myeloma
diagnoses.why: A single plasma cell clone producing paraprotein with osteoclast activation
diagnoses.mimic: MGUS → monoclonal without CRAB or SLiM criteria

diagnoses.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
diagnoses.why: Accumulation of a mature B cell clone over years
diagnoses.mimic: Reactive lymphocytosis → polyclonal, self-limited, infectious context

diagnoses.name: Acute leukemia
diagnoses.why: Marrow replacement by an immature clone crowding out normal lineages
diagnoses.mimic: Leukemoid reaction → left shift without blasts, infectious driver

diagnoses.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
diagnoses.why: Orderly spread through contiguous node groups with systemic cytokine effects
diagnoses.mimic: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma → noncontiguous and frequently extranodal

diagnoses.name: Malignant spinal cord compression
diagnoses.why: Epidural tumor compressing the cord, with axial pain preceding deficits
diagnoses.mimic: Disc herniation → radicular rather than myelopathic, no sensory level

diagnoses.name: Hypercalcemia of malignancy
diagnoses.why: Tumor-driven bone resorption with appropriate feedback suppression of PTH
diagnoses.mimic: Primary hyperparathyroidism → chronic, PTH inappropriately normal or high

diagnoses.name: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.why: Slow-growing head mass obstructing both ducts before causing pain
diagnoses.mimic: Choledocholithiasis → painful, colicky, no mass

diagnoses.name: Superior vena cava syndrome
diagnoses.why: Progressive venous obstruction above the heart
diagnoses.mimic: Heart failure → pulsatile JVP with peripheral edema and orthopnea

diagnoses.name: Sepsis
diagnoses.why: Dysregulated systemic response to infection with perfusion failure
diagnoses.mimic: Adrenal crisis → hypotension responsive to steroid, hyponatremia and hyperkalemia

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing fasciitis
diagnoses.why: Deep fascial infection spreading faster than overlying skin signs develop
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → tenderness proportionate to appearance, slower progression

diagnoses.name: Cellulitis versus erysipelas
diagnoses.why: Depth of infection determines border definition
diagnoses.mimic: Stasis dermatitis → bilateral, chronic, nontender, no fever

diagnoses.name: Vertebral osteomyelitis
diagnoses.why: Blood-borne seeding of vertebral endplates, pain unrelieved by rest
diagnoses.mimic: Mechanical back pain → activity-related, no fever, no night pain

diagnoses.name: Septic arthritis
diagnoses.why: Bacterial invasion of a closed joint space with rapid cartilage destruction. Note the count threshold rules in rather than out: many culture-positive joints have lower counts, so a count below 50,000 does not exclude infection
diagnoses.mimic: Gout → also acute and monoarticular, separated by crystal analysis, and the two can coexist

diagnoses.name: Tuberculosis, reactivation
diagnoses.why: Reactivation in the well-oxygenated apices with endobronchial spread
diagnoses.mimic: Lung cancer → spiculated mass, no tree-in-bud, no fever

diagnoses.name: Meningococcemia
diagnoses.why: Rapid bacteremia with endothelial injury and consumptive coagulopathy
diagnoses.mimic: Viral exanthem → blanching rash, well-appearing

diagnoses.name: Infective endocarditis, acute
diagnoses.why: Virulent organism destroying a valve with septic embolization
diagnoses.mimic: Subacute endocarditis → indolent, constitutional, immune phenomena rather than emboli

diagnoses.name: Acute HIV infection
diagnoses.why: High viremia before antibody development, hence a mononucleosis-like illness
diagnoses.mimic: Infectious mononucleosis → heterophile positive, atypical lymphocytes, no risk exposure

diagnoses.name: Secondary syphilis
diagnoses.why: Hematogenous dissemination of a spirochete with a distinctive acral distribution
diagnoses.mimic: Pityriasis rosea → herald patch, spares palms and soles, pruritic

diagnoses.name: Herpes zoster
diagnoses.why: Reactivation within a single sensory ganglion
diagnoses.mimic: Contact dermatitis → does not respect a dermatome or the midline

diagnoses.name: Infectious mononucleosis
diagnoses.why: Lymphoproliferative viral illness, so the nodes are posterior and the spleen is involved
diagnoses.mimic: Streptococcal pharyngitis → anterior nodes, no splenomegaly, rapid antigen positive

diagnoses.name: Lyme disease, early localized
cluster: with an expanding annular erythema migrans after tick exposure in an endemic area
diagnoses.why: Expanding non-scaling annular lesion at the bite site, a clinical diagnosis
diagnoses.mimic: Tinea corporis → scaling advancing border, no tick exposure, slower

diagnoses.name: Malaria
cluster: paroxysmal fevers with rigors after travel to an endemic area
diagnoses.why: Synchronized parasite release producing periodic fever with cytopenias
diagnoses.mimic: Dengue → no periodicity, retro-orbital pain, leukopenia with rash

diagnoses.name: Infective diarrhea, invasive
diagnoses.why: Mucosal invasion producing blood and systemic response
diagnoses.mimic: Viral gastroenteritis → watery, nonbloody, afebrile or low grade

diagnoses.name: Candidemia
cluster: with a central line and total parenteral nutrition
diagnoses.why: Fungal bloodstream infection in a host with a catheter, so it fails to respond to antibacterials
diagnoses.mimic: Bacterial line infection → responds to antibacterial therapy

diagnoses.name: Prosthetic joint infection
cluster: indolent joint pain with loosening on radiograph and coagulase-negative staphylococci on sonication
diagnoses.why: Biofilm on the implant, so organisms are indolent and cultures need sonication
diagnoses.mimic: Aseptic loosening → normal inflammatory markers, negative cultures

diagnoses.name: Neurosyphilis
cluster: and a reactive CSF treponemal test
diagnoses.why: Tertiary spirochetal infection of the CNS, with a characteristic pupil
diagnoses.mimic: Alzheimer disease → normal CSF serology, no pupillary abnormality

diagnoses.name: Clostridial myonecrosis
cluster: and a thin brown discharge after penetrating injury
diagnoses.why: Toxin-mediated muscle necrosis with gas formation, faster than any other soft tissue infection
diagnoses.mimic: Necrotizing fasciitis → fascial rather than muscle plane, less gas

diagnoses.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
diagnoses.why: Symmetric synovial inflammation sparing the DIPs and eroding at the margins
diagnoses.mimic: Psoriatic arthritis → DIP involvement, dactylitis, asymmetric, nail pitting

diagnoses.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
diagnoses.why: Immune complex disease consuming complement across multiple organs
diagnoses.mimic: Rheumatoid arthritis → erosive, normal complement, anti-CCP positive

diagnoses.name: Psoriatic arthritis
diagnoses.why: Enthesis-centered inflammation rather than synovium-centered
diagnoses.mimic: Rheumatoid arthritis → symmetric, DIP-sparing, seropositive

diagnoses.name: Axial spondyloarthritis
diagnoses.why: Sacroiliac and spinal enthesitis in a young patient, better with movement
diagnoses.mimic: Mechanical back pain → worse with activity, brief stiffness, older onset

diagnoses.name: Gout
diagnoses.why: Urate crystal precipitation triggering explosive neutrophilic inflammation
diagnoses.mimic: Septic arthritis → same acute hot joint; only synovial culture separates them reliably

diagnoses.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
diagnoses.why: Girdle-region inflammation causing pain-limited rather than true weakness
diagnoses.mimic: Inflammatory myopathy → true proximal weakness with raised CK

diagnoses.name: Dermatomyositis
diagnoses.why: Immune-mediated myopathy with a pathognomonic cutaneous signature
diagnoses.mimic: Polymyositis → identical muscle picture without the rash

diagnoses.name: ANCA-associated vasculitis
diagnoses.why: Small-vessel necrotizing inflammation without immune deposits
diagnoses.mimic: Lupus nephritis → low complement, full-house immunofluorescence

diagnoses.name: Systemic sclerosis, diffuse
diagnoses.why: Fibrosis with vasculopathy, extending proximal to elbows and knees
diagnoses.mimic: Limited cutaneous disease → distal only, higher pulmonary hypertension risk, lower renal crisis risk

diagnoses.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and TEN
diagnoses.why: Keratinocyte apoptosis with dermoepidermal separation and mucosal erosion
diagnoses.mimic: DRESS → later onset, facial edema, eosinophilia, organ involvement without Nikolsky

diagnoses.name: DRESS
cluster: Subacute with a 2 to 8 week latency
diagnoses.why: Delayed drug hypersensitivity with organ involvement, the latency being the clue
diagnoses.mimic: Simple morbilliform drug rash → early onset, no organ involvement or eosinophilia

diagnoses.name: Calciphylaxis
diagnoses.why: Medial calcification with luminal occlusion producing branching cutaneous infarcts
diagnoses.mimic: Warfarin-induced necrosis → early in therapy, breast and thigh, protein C related

diagnoses.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
diagnoses.why: Insulin deficiency driving ketogenesis with a gap acidosis
diagnoses.mimic: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state → minimal ketosis, higher glucose, higher osmolality

diagnoses.name: Adrenal insufficiency, primary
diagnoses.why: Loss of both cortisol and aldosterone, with ACTH-driven pigmentation
diagnoses.mimic: Secondary adrenal insufficiency → no hyperkalemia or pigmentation, ACTH low

diagnoses.name: Cushing syndrome, ACTH-independent
diagnoses.why: Autonomous adrenal cortisol production suppressing pituitary ACTH
diagnoses.mimic: Cushing disease → ACTH-dependent, pituitary source, partially suppressible on high dose

diagnoses.name: Graves disease
diagnoses.why: Stimulating antibody driving overproduction, hence high uptake
diagnoses.mimic: Thyroiditis → thyrotoxic with low uptake, tender gland, self-limited

diagnoses.name: Pheochromocytoma
diagnoses.why: Intermittent catecholamine release producing a triad of paroxysmal symptoms
diagnoses.mimic: Panic disorder → no hypertension during episodes, normal metanephrines

diagnoses.name: Primary aldosteronism
diagnoses.why: Autonomous aldosterone with appropriate renin suppression
diagnoses.mimic: Renal artery stenosis → both renin and aldosterone raised

diagnoses.name: SIADH
diagnoses.why: Water retention without volume expansion, hence euvolemia with dilute plasma
diagnoses.mimic: Hypovolemic hyponatremia → clinically dry, low urine sodium, responds to saline

diagnoses.name: Central diabetes insipidus
diagnoses.why: ADH deficiency, so exogenous hormone restores concentration
diagnoses.mimic: Nephrogenic DI → no response to desmopressin, drug or electrolyte cause

diagnoses.name: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
diagnoses.why: Sufficient insulin to suppress ketogenesis but not hyperglycemia, so osmolality dominates
diagnoses.mimic: Diabetic ketoacidosis → anion gap acidosis with ketosis, lower glucose

diagnoses.name: Thyroid storm
diagnoses.why: Decompensated thyrotoxicosis, so systemic failure accompanies the biochemical excess
diagnoses.mimic: Sepsis → no thyroid biochemistry abnormality, no goiter or orbitopathy

diagnoses.name: Myxedema coma
diagnoses.why: Profound hypothyroidism producing multi-system slowing, often precipitated by cold or infection
diagnoses.mimic: Hypothermia from exposure → normal thyroid function, rewarms without hormone

diagnoses.name: Adrenal crisis
diagnoses.why: Mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid deficiency, so pressors fail until steroid is given
diagnoses.mimic: Septic shock → responds to pressors, no hyperkalemia

diagnoses.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
cluster: hypercalcemic with an inappropriately normal or raised PTH
diagnoses.why: Failure of feedback suppression, so PTH is not low when calcium is high
diagnoses.mimic: Hypercalcemia of malignancy → suppressed PTH, raised PTHrP, subacute

diagnoses.name: Subacute thyroiditis
cluster: painful tender goiter with thyrotoxicosis and low radioiodine uptake after a viral illness
diagnoses.why: Release of preformed hormone from a damaged gland, so uptake is low and the gland hurts
diagnoses.mimic: Graves disease → painless, high uptake, orbitopathy

diagnoses.name: Insulinoma
diagnoses.why: Endogenous hyperinsulinemia, so C-peptide is high rather than suppressed
diagnoses.mimic: Exogenous insulin administration → high insulin with suppressed C-peptide

diagnoses.name: Diabetic foot infection
diagnoses.why: Contiguous spread through a neuropathic ulcer, with mixed flora
diagnoses.mimic: Charcot arthropathy → warm swollen deformed foot without ulcer or systemic signs

diagnoses.name: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
cluster: with halos and a fixed mid-dilated pupil
diagnoses.why: Sudden pressure rise in a closed anterior chamber angle, so pain, corneal edema, and pupil paralysis arrive together
diagnoses.mimic: Acute anterior uveitis → painful and red but with a small constricted pupil and normal pressure

diagnoses.name: Central retinal artery occlusion
cluster: complete visual loss with a cherry-red spot
diagnoses.why: Arterial occlusion of the inner retina, so loss is instantaneous and total without inflammation
diagnoses.mimic: Amaurosis fugax → transient, resolves fully within minutes

diagnoses.name: Retinal detachment
diagnoses.why: Mechanical separation producing traction phenomena before field loss
diagnoses.mimic: Vitreous hemorrhage → floaters without a progressing curtain, and no field boundary

diagnoses.name: Optic neuritis
cluster: with an afferent pupillary defect and dyschromatopsia
diagnoses.why: Inflammatory demyelination of the nerve, so pain with movement and color desaturation precede acuity loss
diagnoses.mimic: Ischemic optic neuropathy → painless, older, with altitudinal field loss

diagnoses.name: Giant cell arteritis with visual loss
cluster: Subacute constitutional prodrome then hyperacute monocular painless loss
diagnoses.why: Vasculitic occlusion superimposed on a systemic inflammatory illness, which is why the systemic history precedes the eye
diagnoses.mimic: Non-arteritic ischemic optic neuropathy → no constitutional features, normal inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Acute anterior uveitis
cluster: with ciliary flush and a constricted pupil
diagnoses.why: Anterior chamber inflammation with ciliary spasm, hence photophobia and miosis
diagnoses.mimic: Conjunctivitis → diffuse redness sparing the limbus, no photophobia, normal pupil

diagnoses.name: Bacterial keratitis
cluster: with a corneal infiltrate and contact lens use
diagnoses.why: Corneal epithelial breach with bacterial invasion, so pain is severe and the lesion is visible on the cornea
diagnoses.mimic: Herpes simplex keratitis → dendritic ulcer, reduced corneal sensation

diagnoses.name: Orbital cellulitis
diagnoses.why: Infection posterior to the orbital septum, which is why globe position and motility are affected
diagnoses.mimic: Preseptal cellulitis → no proptosis, no pain on eye movement, normal acuity

diagnoses.name: Endophthalmitis
cluster: with hypopyon after intraocular surgery or injection
diagnoses.why: Intraocular infection following a breach, so the temporal link to a procedure is the clue
diagnoses.mimic: Postoperative inflammation → less pain, no hypopyon, improving rather than worsening

diagnoses.name: Thyroid eye disease
diagnoses.why: Autoimmune orbital infiltration, so proptosis develops slowly and painlessly with lid signs
diagnoses.mimic: Orbital cellulitis → acute, painful, febrile, unilateral

diagnoses.name: Peritonsillar abscess
diagnoses.why: A collection lateral to the tonsil displaces structures, which is why the findings are asymmetric
diagnoses.mimic: Streptococcal pharyngitis → bilateral, no trismus, no uvular deviation

diagnoses.name: Epiglottitis
cluster: with odynophagia out of proportion to exam
diagnoses.why: Supraglottic swelling threatening the airway before the oropharynx looks abnormal
diagnoses.mimic: Peritonsillar abscess → visible asymmetry on oropharyngeal exam

diagnoses.name: Ludwig angina
cluster: bilateral submandibular induration with tongue elevation and a dental source
diagnoses.why: Bilateral floor-of-mouth cellulitis pushing the tongue upward and backward
diagnoses.mimic: Submandibular sialadenitis → unilateral, related to eating, no tongue elevation

diagnoses.name: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss
cluster: painless hearing loss with Weber lateralizing to the good ear
diagnoses.why: Cochlear or retrocochlear failure, so lateralization is away from the affected side
diagnoses.mimic: Cerumen impaction or effusion → conductive, Weber lateralizes to the affected ear

diagnoses.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
cluster: positional vertigo lasting under a minute with fatigable nystagmus
diagnoses.why: Otolith debris in a semicircular canal, so symptoms are provoked by position and brief
diagnoses.mimic: Vestibular neuritis → constant for days rather than seconds, not position-triggered

diagnoses.name: Vestibular neuritis
cluster: constant vertigo for days with direction-fixed nystagmus and an abnormal head impulse test
diagnoses.why: Peripheral vestibular inflammation, so the vestibulo-ocular reflex fails on the affected side
diagnoses.mimic: Cerebellar stroke → direction-changing nystagmus, normal head impulse, skew deviation

diagnoses.name: Nasal septal hematoma
diagnoses.why: Blood between septal cartilage and perichondrium, which devascularizes cartilage within days
diagnoses.mimic: Simple septal deviation → chronic, non-tender, no fluctuance

diagnoses.name: Malignant otitis externa
cluster: severe otalgia in a diabetic with granulation tissue at the bony junction
diagnoses.why: Skull-base osteomyelitis from Pseudomonas, so pain outlasts and outweighs the canal findings
diagnoses.mimic: Uncomplicated otitis externa → resolves with topical therapy, no cranial nerve involvement

diagnoses.name: Testicular torsion
cluster: severe scrotal pain with a high-riding transverse testis and absent cremasteric reflex
diagnoses.why: Cord twisting causes ischemia within hours, so onset is abrupt and the testis changes position
diagnoses.mimic: Epididymitis → gradual onset, relief on elevation, preserved cremasteric reflex

diagnoses.name: Epididymitis
cluster: unilateral scrotal pain relieved by elevation
diagnoses.why: Ascending infection along the vas, so urinary symptoms accompany and elevation helps
diagnoses.mimic: Testicular torsion → hyperacute, elevation does not help, cremasteric reflex absent

diagnoses.name: Nephrolithiasis
cluster: unilateral flank pain radiating to the groin
diagnoses.why: Ureteric obstruction with peristalsis working against it, hence waves and radiation along the ureter
diagnoses.mimic: Pyelonephritis → febrile, constant rather than colicky, costovertebral tenderness

diagnoses.name: Acute pyelonephritis
cluster: unilateral flank pain with pyuria and positive culture
diagnoses.why: Ascending infection reaching the renal parenchyma, so systemic features accompany local ones
diagnoses.mimic: Cystitis → afebrile, no flank pain, symptoms confined to voiding

diagnoses.name: Acute urinary retention
cluster: suprapubic pain with a palpable bladder and inability to void
diagnoses.why: Mechanical or neurogenic outflow failure, relieved immediately by catheter
diagnoses.mimic: Anuria from renal failure → no bladder distension, catheter yields nothing

diagnoses.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
cluster: progressive obstructive voiding symptoms with hesitancy and a weak stream
diagnoses.why: Slowly progressive outflow narrowing, so storage symptoms follow obstruction over years
diagnoses.mimic: Prostate carcinoma → often asymptomatic until advanced, nodular on examination

diagnoses.name: Fournier gangrene
cluster: rapidly progressive perineal pain out of proportion to exam
diagnoses.why: Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum, where fascial spread outruns skin signs
diagnoses.mimic: Scrotal cellulitis → tenderness proportionate, no crepitus, slower course

diagnoses.name: Renal cell carcinoma
cluster: painless hematuria with a hypervascular heterogeneous renal mass
diagnoses.why: Slow-growing hypervascular tumor, so bleeding is painless and imaging is characteristic
diagnoses.mimic: Angiomyolipoma → macroscopic fat on imaging, benign

diagnoses.name: Bladder carcinoma
cluster: intermittent hematuria in a smoker over 40
diagnoses.why: Urothelial malignancy bleeds without pain and intermittently, which delays presentation
diagnoses.mimic: Cystitis → painful, febrile or dysuric, positive culture

diagnoses.name: Priapism, ischemic
cluster: persistent erection with rigid corpora and low-flow blood gas
diagnoses.why: Veno-occlusive compartment syndrome of the penis, so it is painful and time-critical
diagnoses.mimic: Non-ischemic priapism → painless, semi-rigid, follows trauma

diagnoses.name: Phimosis with paraphimosis
cluster: painful glans swelling with a retracted foreskin acting as a constricting band
diagnoses.why: A retracted tight ring obstructs venous return distal to it
diagnoses.mimic: Balanitis → no constricting band, foreskin reducible

diagnoses.name: Renal infarction
cluster: unilateral flank pain with very high LDH and a wedge-shaped perfusion defect
diagnoses.why: Arterial occlusion of a renal segment, so pain is abrupt and enzymes rise without infection
diagnoses.mimic: Nephrolithiasis → colicky rather than constant, stone on imaging

diagnoses.name: Ectopic pregnancy
diagnoses.why: Implantation outside the uterus, so the pregnancy test is positive while the uterus is empty
diagnoses.mimic: Threatened miscarriage → intrauterine sac present, bleeding without lateralized pain

diagnoses.name: Ovarian torsion
cluster: severe pelvic pain with an adnexal mass and absent Doppler flow
diagnoses.why: Vascular pedicle twisting, so pain is abrupt and out of proportion with a palpable mass
diagnoses.mimic: Ruptured ovarian cyst → sudden pain that eases, free fluid, preserved flow

diagnoses.name: Preeclampsia with severe features
diagnoses.why: Placental-driven endothelial dysfunction, which is why hypertension and proteinuria arrive together with neurologic symptoms
diagnoses.mimic: Chronic hypertension → predates 20 weeks, no proteinuria or end-organ features

diagnoses.name: HELLP syndrome
diagnoses.why: Microangiopathy in the liver and marrow, so right upper quadrant pain accompanies the laboratory triad
diagnoses.mimic: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy → hypoglycemia and coagulopathy dominate, platelets less affected

diagnoses.name: Placental abruption
cluster: painful vaginal bleeding with a tense uterus and fetal distress
diagnoses.why: Retroplacental hemorrhage separating the placenta, so the uterus is rigid and tender
diagnoses.mimic: Placenta previa → painless bleeding with a soft uterus

diagnoses.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
cluster: heavy bleeding after delivery with a boggy uterus
diagnoses.why: Uterine atony is the commonest cause, so the uterus fails to contract down
diagnoses.mimic: Retained products → bleeding with a contracted uterus and retained tissue on imaging

diagnoses.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
cluster: bilateral lower abdominal pain with cervical motion tenderness and discharge
diagnoses.why: Ascending infection of the upper genital tract, so tenderness is bilateral and cervical
diagnoses.mimic: Appendicitis → migratory, localized to the right lower quadrant, no cervical motion tenderness

diagnoses.name: Endometriosis
diagnoses.why: Ectopic endometrium responding to cyclic hormones, hence pain tied to the menstrual cycle
diagnoses.mimic: Adenomyosis → diffusely enlarged tender uterus, heavy bleeding rather than cyclical focal pain

diagnoses.name: Ovarian carcinoma
diagnoses.why: Peritoneal spread before local symptoms, which is why presentation is late and vague
diagnoses.mimic: Benign ovarian cyst → simple on imaging, no ascites, no constitutional features

diagnoses.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
cluster: persistent vomiting in early pregnancy with ketosis and weight loss over 5%
diagnoses.why: Severity beyond ordinary morning sickness, defined by metabolic consequences
diagnoses.mimic: Ordinary nausea of pregnancy → no ketosis, no weight loss, no electrolyte disturbance

diagnoses.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
cluster: Hyperacute cardiovascular collapse during or just after labour
diagnoses.why: Catastrophic anaphylactoid response, so collapse and coagulopathy are simultaneous
diagnoses.mimic: Pulmonary embolism → collapse without early disseminated intravascular coagulation

diagnoses.name: Chorioamnionitis
diagnoses.why: Intra-amniotic infection ascending after membrane rupture, so fever and fetal tachycardia coincide
diagnoses.mimic: Urinary tract infection in pregnancy → no uterine tenderness, no fetal tachycardia

diagnoses.name: Major depressive episode
cluster: and neurovegetative change over at least two weeks
diagnoses.why: Duration plus anhedonia plus somatic features distinguish it from ordinary sadness
diagnoses.mimic: Adjustment disorder → tied to an identifiable stressor, resolves as it does

diagnoses.name: Bipolar mania
cluster: episodic elevated or irritable mood with reduced sleep need and goal-directed overactivity
diagnoses.why: Reduced need for sleep, rather than insomnia with fatigue, is the discriminating feature
diagnoses.mimic: Stimulant intoxication → toxicology positive, resolves with abstinence

diagnoses.name: Serotonin syndrome
cluster: and autonomic instability after a serotonergic drug
diagnoses.why: Neuromuscular excitability appears within hours of a drug change, and is greater in the legs
diagnoses.mimic: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome → lead-pipe rigidity, hyporeflexia, slower onset

diagnoses.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
cluster: and a very high creatine kinase
diagnoses.why: Dopamine blockade producing rigidity rather than hyperreflexia, over days
diagnoses.mimic: Serotonin syndrome → clonus and hyperreflexia, onset in hours

diagnoses.name: Alcohol withdrawal
cluster: 6 to 72 hours after the last drink
diagnoses.why: The timing relative to the last drink is the defining feature
diagnoses.mimic: Delirium from another cause → no temporal link to cessation, no early tremor

diagnoses.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
cluster: and ataxia in a thiamine-depleted patient
diagnoses.why: Thiamine deficiency injuring periaqueductal structures, producing a specific triad
diagnoses.mimic: Alcohol intoxication → resolves with time, no ophthalmoplegia

diagnoses.name: Catatonia
diagnoses.why: A motor syndrome of psychiatric or medical origin, responsive to benzodiazepines
diagnoses.mimic: Depressive stupor → no waxy flexibility or echophenomena

diagnoses.name: Anorexia nervosa
cluster: progressive restriction with low body weight and intense fear of weight gain
diagnoses.why: Restriction driven by body image rather than appetite loss, in the presence of medical sequelae
diagnoses.mimic: Malignancy-related cachexia → no fear of weight gain, appetite preserved or lost involuntarily

diagnoses.name: Somatic symptom disorder
cluster: persistent physical symptoms with disproportionate thoughts
diagnoses.why: Defined by the response to symptoms rather than by whether the symptoms are explained
diagnoses.mimic: Functional neurological disorder → positive signs of internal inconsistency on examination

diagnoses.name: Acute psychosis, first episode
diagnoses.why: New psychosis in a young adult, requiring organic causes to be excluded first
diagnoses.mimic: Delirium → fluctuating attention and a global rather than a thought-content disturbance

diagnoses.name: Acetaminophen overdose
cluster: then hepatocellular injury with aminotransferases above 1000 at 24 to 72 hours
diagnoses.why: The asymptomatic latent phase is the trap, because presentation is normal when treatment works best
diagnoses.mimic: Ischaemic hepatitis → shock precedes, transaminases fall as rapidly as they rose

diagnoses.name: Salicylate toxicity
cluster: and a mixed respiratory alkalosis with raised anion gap metabolic acidosis
diagnoses.why: Simultaneous direct respiratory stimulation and metabolic acidosis, a nearly unique combination
diagnoses.mimic: Diabetic ketoacidosis → pure anion gap acidosis with compensatory hyperventilation, no tinnitus

diagnoses.name: Toxic alcohol ingestion
cluster: with a raised anion gap and a raised osmolar gap
diagnoses.why: Two gaps together indicate an unmeasured small osmotically active acid precursor
diagnoses.mimic: Alcoholic ketoacidosis → raised anion gap without an osmolar gap

diagnoses.name: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose
cluster: and a terminal R wave in aVR
diagnoses.why: Sodium channel blockade widening the QRS, which predicts seizures and arrhythmia
diagnoses.mimic: Antihistamine overdose → anticholinergic without QRS widening

diagnoses.name: Opioid toxicity
cluster: with a depressed level of consciousness
diagnoses.why: The triad reflects central mu-receptor effects, and reverses with naloxone
diagnoses.mimic: Sedative-hypnotic overdose → normal pupils, no response to naloxone

diagnoses.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
cluster: Acute or subacute headache and confusion with a normal oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry
diagnoses.why: Carboxyhemoglobin is read as oxyhemoglobin, so the saturation is falsely reassuring
diagnoses.mimic: Viral illness → no co-exposure history, no cluster of affected household members

diagnoses.name: Sympathomimetic toxidrome
diagnoses.why: Adrenergic excess with intact sweating, which separates it from anticholinergic states
diagnoses.mimic: Anticholinergic toxidrome → dry skin, urinary retention, absent bowel sounds

diagnoses.name: Anticholinergic toxidrome
diagnoses.why: Muscarinic blockade producing dryness, which is the discriminating feature
diagnoses.mimic: Sympathomimetic toxidrome → diaphoretic rather than dry

diagnoses.name: Digoxin toxicity
diagnoses.why: Sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition producing both the arrhythmia and the potassium shift
diagnoses.mimic: Hyperkalemia from other causes → no visual symptoms, no characteristic arrhythmia

diagnoses.name: Beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose
cluster: with hyperglycemia pointing to calcium channel blockade
diagnoses.why: Both cause bradycardia and hypotension; glucose separates them, since beta blockade tends to hypoglycemia
diagnoses.mimic: Digoxin toxicity → bradycardia with hyperkalemia and characteristic ectopy

diagnoses.name: Serotonergic drug interaction
cluster: with clonus greater in the legs
diagnoses.why: Onset within hours of a drug change, with lower-limb-predominant clonus
diagnoses.mimic: Malignant hyperthermia → follows an anesthetic trigger, with masseter spasm

diagnoses.name: Methemoglobinemia
cluster: Acute cyanosis with a saturation gap and chocolate-brown blood not correcting on oxygen
diagnoses.why: Hemoglobin locked in the ferric state, so oxygen does not help and the blood color changes
diagnoses.mimic: Shunt physiology → cyanosis without a saturation gap or abnormal blood color

diagnoses.name: Psoriasis, plaque
cluster: well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale and nail pitting
diagnoses.why: Extensor distribution with sharp borders and nail change, the mirror image of eczema
diagnoses.mimic: Atopic dermatitis → flexural, ill-defined, lichenified, intensely pruritic

diagnoses.name: Atopic dermatitis
cluster: lichenified plaques with a personal or family atopic history
diagnoses.why: Itch-scratch cycle in flexures, producing thickening rather than scale
diagnoses.mimic: Psoriasis → extensor, sharply demarcated, silvery scale

diagnoses.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
cluster: flaccid bullae with Nikolsky positivity and prominent mucosal erosions
diagnoses.why: Intraepidermal split from desmoglein antibodies, so blisters are flaccid and mucosa is involved early
diagnoses.mimic: Bullous pemphigoid → tense bullae, mucosa usually spared, older patient

diagnoses.name: Bullous pemphigoid
cluster: tense bullae on urticarial plaques in an older patient
diagnoses.why: Subepidermal split, so blisters are tense and roof-intact
diagnoses.mimic: Pemphigus vulgaris → flaccid bullae with mucosal disease

diagnoses.name: Cellulitis
diagnoses.why: Deeper dermal and subcutaneous infection, so margins blur into normal skin
diagnoses.mimic: Erysipelas → sharply demarcated, raised border, more abrupt onset

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing fasciitis, cutaneous presentation
cluster: pain out of proportion to exam
diagnoses.why: Fascial plane infection outrunning skin findings, which is why the exam underestimates it
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → tenderness proportionate to appearance, slower progression

diagnoses.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
cluster: medication-induced with a 1 to 3 week latency
diagnoses.why: Widespread keratinocyte apoptosis with mucosal involvement, timed to a new drug
diagnoses.mimic: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome → mucosa spared, superficial split, young child

diagnoses.name: Erythema multiforme
diagnoses.why: True targets with three concentric zones on hands and feet
diagnoses.mimic: Urticaria multiforme → transient annular wheals, individual lesions under 24 hours

diagnoses.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
cluster: rapidly enlarging painful ulcer with a violaceous undermined border and pathergy
diagnoses.why: Neutrophilic dermatosis, so trauma worsens it and debridement is harmful
diagnoses.mimic: Infected ulcer → responds to antibiotics, no undermined violaceous edge

diagnoses.name: Melanoma
diagnoses.why: Change over time in an asymmetric pigmented lesion is the discriminating feature
diagnoses.mimic: Seborrhoeic keratosis → stuck-on, waxy, symmetric, stable

diagnoses.name: Basal cell carcinoma
cluster: slowly enlarging pearly papule with telangiectasia and a rolled border on sun-exposed skin
diagnoses.why: Very slow local growth without metastasis, on cumulative sun damage
diagnoses.mimic: Squamous cell carcinoma → faster, keratotic, may be tender, can metastasize

diagnoses.name: Scabies
cluster: with burrows in finger webs and household contacts affected
diagnoses.why: Nocturnal itch with linear burrows and a contact history is close to specific
diagnoses.mimic: Atopic dermatitis → flexural, no burrows, no contact clustering

diagnoses.name: Erythroderma
cluster: generalized erythema involving over 90% of the skin
diagnoses.why: Extent itself becomes the problem, causing fluid and temperature loss regardless of cause
diagnoses.mimic: Extensive drug eruption → under 90%, no thermoregulatory compromise

diagnoses.name: Cutaneous drug eruption, morbilliform
cluster: 4 to 14 days after a new drug
diagnoses.why: Timing to drug exposure with sparing of mucosa and organs
diagnoses.mimic: DRESS → facial edema, eosinophilia, hepatitis, longer latency

diagnoses.name: Compartment syndrome
cluster: pain out of proportion to exam with pain on passive stretch and a tense compartment
diagnoses.why: Rising compartment pressure, where pain and passive stretch precede pulselessness
diagnoses.mimic: Deep vein thrombosis → no pain on passive stretch, no compartment tension

diagnoses.name: Hip fracture
cluster: unilateral inability to weight bear with a shortened externally rotated leg after a fall
diagnoses.why: Mechanical discontinuity producing a characteristic limb position
diagnoses.mimic: Hip contusion → able to weight bear, no deformity, normal radiograph

diagnoses.name: Osteoarthritis
cluster: activity-related joint pain with brief gelling and bony enlargement
diagnoses.why: Worse with use and better with rest, the mirror image of inflammatory arthritis
diagnoses.mimic: Rheumatoid arthritis → inflammatory, morning stiffness over an hour, symmetric small joints

diagnoses.name: Rotator cuff tear
cluster: activity-related shoulder pain with weakness on external rotation and a positive drop arm
diagnoses.why: Structural tendon failure producing weakness rather than only pain
diagnoses.mimic: Adhesive capsulitis → restricted passive as well as active range

diagnoses.name: Adhesive capsulitis
cluster: progressive shoulder stiffness with equally restricted active and passive range
diagnoses.why: Capsular contracture limits passive movement, which tendon disease does not
diagnoses.mimic: Rotator cuff tear → passive range preserved

diagnoses.name: Lumbar disc herniation
cluster: radicular leg pain in a dermatome with a positive straight leg raise
diagnoses.why: Root compression producing dermatomal pain with a reproducible tension sign
diagnoses.mimic: Spinal stenosis → neurogenic claudication relieved by flexion, bilateral

diagnoses.name: Lumbar spinal stenosis
