cluster: progressive neurogenic claudication relieved by sitting or leaning forward
diagnoses.why: Canal narrowing that eases when the spine flexes, unlike vascular claudication
diagnoses.mimic: Vascular claudication → relieved by standing still, absent pulses

diagnoses.name: Septic bursitis
cluster: localized swelling over a bursa with overlying erythema and preserved joint range
diagnoses.why: Infection confined to the bursa, so the joint itself moves normally
diagnoses.mimic: Septic arthritis → joint range severely restricted and painful

diagnoses.name: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture
cluster: midline thoracolumbar pain after minimal trauma with focal tenderness and loss of height
diagnoses.why: Fragility fracture, so the mechanism is trivial relative to the injury
diagnoses.mimic: Malignant infiltration → night pain, constitutional features, lytic lesion

diagnoses.name: Achilles tendon rupture
cluster: and absent plantarflexion on calf squeeze
diagnoses.why: Complete tendon discontinuity abolishes the Thompson test
diagnoses.mimic: Achilles tendinopathy → activity-related pain with an intact Thompson test

diagnoses.name: Cauda equina from disc
diagnoses.why: Compression of multiple lumbosacral roots, a time-critical surgical emergency
diagnoses.mimic: Unilateral radiculopathy → no saddle involvement, no sphincter disturbance

diagnoses.name: Osteomyelitis, diabetic foot
cluster: indolent ulcer with probe-to-bone positivity and raised inflammatory markers
diagnoses.why: Contiguous spread from an overlying ulcer, so the ulcer precedes the bone disease
diagnoses.mimic: Neuropathic ulcer without osteomyelitis → probe-to-bone negative, normal markers

diagnoses.name: Deep vein thrombosis
cluster: unilateral leg swelling with calf tenderness and a measured circumference difference over 3 cm
diagnoses.why: Unilaterality plus measurement, since bilateral swelling points systemic
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → erythema and warmth predominate, fever more common

diagnoses.name: Acute limb ischemia
diagnoses.why: Sudden arterial occlusion producing the six-P sequence within hours
diagnoses.mimic: Critical limb ischemia → chronic, rest pain over weeks, collaterals present

diagnoses.name: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
diagnoses.why: Rupture producing pain plus shock plus a palpable expansile mass together
diagnoses.mimic: Renal colic → colicky, hemodynamically stable, stone on imaging

diagnoses.name: Superficial thrombophlebitis
cluster: with a tender palpable cord along a superficial vein and localized erythema
diagnoses.why: Thrombosis of a superficial vein, so the cord is palpable and linear
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → diffuse rather than linear, no palpable cord

diagnoses.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
cluster: bilateral dependent edema with hemosiderin staining and medial malleolar ulceration
diagnoses.why: Venous hypertension over years producing pigmentation and a characteristic ulcer site
diagnoses.mimic: Arterial ulcer → lateral or distal, punched out, painful, absent pulses

diagnoses.name: Lymphedema
cluster: nonpitting limb swelling with a positive Stemmer sign and skin thickening
diagnoses.why: Protein-rich interstitial fluid, so it does not pit and the skin thickens
diagnoses.mimic: Venous edema → pitting, improves overnight, pigmentation rather than thickening

diagnoses.name: Carotid stenosis
cluster: or transient monocular visual loss and contralateral hemispheric symptoms
diagnoses.why: Territorial symptoms match the vessel, which is why the eye and the opposite hemisphere pair
diagnoses.mimic: Vertebrobasilar disease → bilateral or posterior symptoms, no monocular loss

diagnoses.name: Takayasu arteritis
diagnoses.why: Large-vessel inflammation in a young patient, so pulses and pressures differ between limbs
diagnoses.mimic: Atherosclerotic disease → older, no constitutional features, normal inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Anaphylaxis
cluster: with airway compromise and hypotension after an exposure
diagnoses.why: Two or more organ systems within minutes of a trigger, which no other reaction does
diagnoses.mimic: Vasovagal syncope → bradycardic, pallor without urticaria, rapid spontaneous recovery

diagnoses.name: Hereditary angiedema
cluster: nonpruritic angiedema without urticaria and unresponsive to antihistamines
diagnoses.why: Bradykinin-mediated, so there is no urticaria and no response to antihistamine or adrenaline
diagnoses.mimic: Histaminergic angiedema → urticarial, pruritic, responds to antihistamine

diagnoses.name: Chronic spontaneous urticaria
cluster: recurrent wheals with individual lesions resolving under 24 hours and no identified trigger
diagnoses.why: Duration of the individual lesion is the discriminator, not the duration of the illness
diagnoses.mimic: Urticarial vasculitis → lesions lasting over 24 hours, bruising, burning rather than itching

diagnoses.name: Drug-induced anaphylactoid reaction
cluster: clinically identical to anaphylaxis but without prior sensitization
diagnoses.why: Direct mast cell activation, so it can occur on first exposure
diagnoses.mimic: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis → requires prior sensitization

diagnoses.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
cluster: recurrent sinopulmonary infection with low immunoglobulins and poor vaccine response
diagnoses.why: Antibody failure producing encapsulated organism infection and bronchiectasis over years
diagnoses.mimic: Cystic fibrosis → sweat chloride positive, pancreatic insufficiency, earlier onset

diagnoses.name: Mastocytosis
cluster: and hypotension with a raised baseline tryptase
diagnoses.why: Mast cell burden producing paroxysmal mediator release between attacks
diagnoses.mimic: Carcinoid syndrome → flushing with diarrhea and raised urinary 5-HIAA
